articleTitle: Enhancing Performance of Bidirectional Charging System for V2G and G2V in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Enhancing grid stability and efficiency can be achieved by integrating renewable energy sources (REs), such as solar and wind power (PV), with the electrical system. This research paper explores the optimization of bidirectional charging systems for Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) and Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) interactions in a smart power grid framework. By leveraging bidirectional charging technology, electric vehicles (EVs) can both consume energy from the grid and return surplus electricity to it during peak demand, thereby supporting grid balancing and reducing dependence on non-renewable sources. Our study focuses on the performance enhancement of these systems by analyzing various integration strategies with renewable energy sources. We propose effective approaches to improve the efficiency of energy transfer, manage energy storage, and ensure stable grid operation. Simulation results demonstrate significant improvements in system reliability, energy utilization, and cost-effectiveness. The results emphasize the potential of advanced bidirectional charging systems to optimize renewable energy utilization and support a more resilient, sustainable smart grid infrastructure.

articleTitle: Model-Free Predictive Current Control for Induction Motor Drive Using Recursive Least Squares Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: A conventional model predictive current control (MPCC) scheme for an induction motor (IM) drive performs as an effective controller at dynamic and steady-state conditions. However, the performance of this control scheme is highly dependent on the mismatch in the motor parameters. In addition, the modeling knowledge of the IM and its accurate parameters measurement are required in the controller. In this paper, a new model-free PCC (MF-PCC) scheme has been proposed to overcome the aforementioned problems. The proposed scheme uses an auto-regressive exogenous (ARX) model instead of the motor model to form a model-free controller. The ARX model works only on the motor's input-output transfer function. The unknown coefficients or parameters in the ARX model are estimated by using a recursive least squares algorithm. To obtain an accurate prediction, an ARX structure has been modified into an observable canonical state-space model. Simulation results show that the proposed control scheme is robust against motor parameters mismatch under different operating conditions in comparison with the conventional MPCC scheme.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Wind Power Prediction for Electric Vehicle Charging Hour Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Renewable energy is the future of power generation and wind power is one of the important players in meeting the energy demand that is continuously increasing with the innovation of new technology like electric vehicles (EVs). In this paper, a machine learning-based approach has been considered to tackle the increased energy demand by predicting EVs' most convenient charging hour by renewable energy source. A wind turbine power generation dataset has been considered to predict power generation throughout the year. The study has been done in two parts, firstly we have applied ML algorithms and secondly, we have done time series analysis. Five ML algorithms have been used to compare the accuracy, correlation, and different types of errors. Among the five ML algorithms, XGB Regressor provided the best predictions for wind power generation to schedule EV charging with an accuracy of 98.17%. On the other hand, our time series study reveals that charging EVs between 1 AM to 6 AM is the most effective time for utilizing wind power and addressing energy demand.

articleTitle: Exploring Sleep Disorders: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms on Sleep Health and Lifestyle Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Classifying sleep disorders is crucial for improving human health, as conditions like apnea significantly impact well-being. Traditional methods are often error-prone, necessitating accurate machine learning algorithms (MLAs). This research compares several MLAs using the Sleep Health and Lifestyle Dataset. The dataset is processed by label encoding variables such as gender, occupation, blood pressure, and BMI category, followed by MinMax scaling for normalization. It is splitted into training, testing, and validation sets. K-fold cross-validation is utilized for reliable performance estimation, and hyperparameter tuning is conducted to enhance model accuracy. The parameters tuned include the number of estimators, learning rate, and maximum depth for algorithms like Random Forest, AdaBoost, and Gradient Boosting. Our findings indicate that Gradient Boosting achieved the highest classification accuracy at 93.80%, outperforming Random Forest (90.26%), Logistic Regression (91.15%), and AdaBoost (91.15%). Gradient Boosting's superior performance is attributed to its ability to sequentially build and optimize weak learners, effectively capturing complex patterns in the data. This study underscores the effectiveness of optimized MLAs in accurately classifying sleep disorders, emphasizing the importance of thorough preprocessing and hyperparameter tuning.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Feature Extraction Network for COVID-19 Classification Based on Chest X-Ray Images Using LGBM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The COVID-19 outbreak stands as one of the most significant global health crises in recent memory, claiming millions of lives worldwide. The urgent and precise identification of the disease holds paramount importance for effective treatment and preventive measures due to its rapid spread. Moreover, distinguishing between COVID-19 and other pneumonia ailments is crucial for accurate diagnosis and subsequent treatment, given their similar symptomatology and physiological impacts. Leveraging x-ray imaging in medical diagnostics offers a rapid and cost-effective means of detection. In this study, a dual-stage feature selection methodology is employed on hybrid or combined deep convolutional characteristics or features extracted from x-ray images. Three convolutional neural networks (CNNs) - Inception V3,ResNet50, and Xception - are utilized in a transfer learning framework. The performance of combining features from multiple CNNs is meticulously analyzed. Initially, features from various models are selected at a specified percentage in the first level of feature selection, followed by a second level to identify the most informative features. Both levels employ the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM) algorithm for selection. The resultant feature set is then utilized to classify Viral Pneumonia, COVID-19 and non-Covid-19 chest x-ray images using a Support Vector Machines (SVM) classifier. The proposed model's efficacy is evaluated using an open-access dataset, achieving a peak accuracy of 98.49% by leveraging only 35% of the features extracted from the proposed hybrid model consisting of ResNet50, InceptionV3,and Xception networks.

articleTitle: Analyzing Spatial Consistency and Human Blockage in mmWave Channel Modeling within Metrorail Scenarios in Next Generation Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The advent of 5G technology promises transformative capabilities to meet the escalating demands of modern connectivity. Among its key enablers, millimeter-wave (mmWave) spectrum stands out for its potential to deliver unprecedented data speeds and capacity. Integrating mmWave technology into 5G networks presents unique challenges and opportunities, particularly in complex urban environments such as metro rail scenarios. Channel modeling plays a pivotal role in understanding signal propagation dynamics within these environments, guiding the design and optimization of next-generation networks. This study investigates spatial consistency and human blockage effects in mmWave channel modeling within metro rail settings, employing advanced simulation techniques to shed light on the intricacies of signal propagation and system performance. The findings offer valuable insights for enhancing mmWave integration in 5G networks, paving the way for efficient and reliable connectivity in urban transit environments.

articleTitle: Vehicle Charging with Net Metering and Protection System: A Regional Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The number of electric vehicles (EVs) has increased recently, necessitating the demand for additional EV charging stations. In Bangladesh, the number of electric vehicles, such as autorickshaws and electric motorcycles are growing daily. Electric motorcycles and autorickshaws in Bangladesh are powered by energy drawn from the national grid. This project focuses on the construction of a PV based EV charging station with net metering and a hazard protection system for external battery in order to reduce the strain on the national grid and make use of renewable energy. The goal of this project is to design and build an electric vehicle charging system that provides a reliable way to charge electric motorcycle, autorickshaw's battery and other electric vehicles by using solar energy as renewable source.

articleTitle: Remote-Controlled Robotic Arm Using RF Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In response to the escalating demand for precise and versatile robotic solutions in industrial automation, this project introduces an innovative system that goes beyond conventional standards—an RF (Radio Frequency) remote-controlled robotic arm. The core objective of this research is to address the burgeoning industrial requirements by designing, developing, and evaluating a robotic arm endowed with six degrees of freedom (6-DOF), empowering it to execute intricate tasks with unprecedented precision and flexibility under remote human control. The project's foundational components include a meticulously designed robotic arm with 6-DOF capabilities, RF communication modules, and an intuitive remote control interface. The incorporation of 6-DOF allows the robotic arm to mimic the nuanced movements of a human arm, offering enhanced dexterity and adaptability in handling a diverse array of industrial tasks. This expanded range of motion enables the robotic arm to navigate and manipulate objects in three-dimensional space with greater agility and accuracy. Harnessing the capabilities of RF technology, the system facilitates real-time, wireless communication between the operator and the robotic arm, enabling seamless remote task execution. The findings of this research highlight the system's effectiveness in precisely replicating human arm movements, resulting in responsive and intuitive control. In-depth testing and analysis underscore the system's reliability, showcasing minimal latency and robust signal transmission-attributes crucial for its applicability across a broad spectrum of industrial scenarios. This RF remote-controlled robotic arm, with its 6-DOF design, emerges as a cutting-edge solution poised to revolutionize industrial automation. Its capacity to execute intricate tasks remotely with remarkable accuracy, combined with the adaptability conferred by 6-DOF, positions it as a versatile tool capable of meeting the evolving challenges of modern industrial environments.

articleTitle: Grid-Connected Generating Unit with an Efficient Stabilization Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This article explores how H ∞ control can improve the stability and responsiveness of a Single Machine Infinite Bus (SMIB) system. Controlling SMIB system is essential for stability maintenance, voltage and frequency regulation, load balancing, mitigation of disturbances, and optimization of system performances of power transmission and distribution networks. To solve these problems, H ∞ controller works against real-world uncertainty, resulting in a more robust controller for the SMIB system in this regard. Designing an H ∞ controller with altered weights will maximize system response. Also, it will effectively alleviate system disruptions and variations which are major factors in low-frequency oscillations of the system for the load deviations. To assess the proposed controller's dynamic behavior and enhance system stability, a single machine is inter-faced with an infinite bus. The SMIB system's parameters are specified, including damping coefficients, synchronous reactance, active power, reactive power, and other relevant variables. The system's stability is examined and a stability correction factor is introduced to enhance the representation of system dynamics. The SMIB system's state-space model is then developed in MAT-LAB to make controller design and simulation easier. Control performance is compared to conventional PID and LQR optimal control schemes. The results demonstrate that the suggested controller is robust across various operating circumstances over other experimental controllers.

articleTitle: Eighth-Mode Cavity-Backed Antenna Using SIW Technology for Wireless Body Area Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In this paper, a cavity-backed antenna operating at the eighth mode of its fundamental frequency is proposed employing substrate integrated waveguide technology, for the wireless body area network application. The eighth-mode concept is employed to reduce size by 1/8 times of its original size and make the antenna conformal while functioning close to the human body. The antenna operates at 2.4GHz ISM-band of frequency spectrum with a minimum SAR value of 0.0315W/kg for 1gm of tissue. The proposed antenna exhibits good impedance matching while loaded on body having minimum bandwidth of 48 MHz with a well-directed superior positive gain of 6.5dBi. This eighth-mode concept further conduces to reduce production cost and complexity. The effect of its ground plane was also examined in this paper and presented to specific absorption rate (SAR). The CST Microwave Studio was employed to carry out simulation.

articleTitle: Potential Charging Techniques for Electric Vehicles Utilizing Photovoltaic Sources in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Most of the vehicles in Bangladesh are operated by fossil fuels such as petrol, octane, compressed natural gas, etc. This leads to the emission of a huge amount of greenhouse gases. Besides, most of these fuels are imported, which is a big challenge for energy security. Also, the prices of these fuels are increasing day by day. As a result, the maintenance cost of these vehicles also increased. The abovementioned problems can be solved using electric vehicles (EVs) instead of conventional vehicles. However, charging the batteries of EVs using the conventional grid-to-vehicle charging mechanism presents a huge burden on the national grid. Also, at present, there are no government laws regulating the charging of EVs using the national grid. As a result, there is enormous motivation to explore the possibility of charging EVs using alternative sources. This paper discusses electric vehicles and their charging techniques using photovoltaic (PV) sources. In the MATLAB/Simulink framework, two separate charging systems-the PV grid and the PV standalone-are investigated and simulated. The simulation results confirm the validity of the two charging techniques and show that about 3.45%-4.74% burden can be reduced from the national grid per day by charging the EVs via the two techniques.

articleTitle: Harmonizing Denoising and Color Preservation with Attention-Infused AutoEncoder for Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study introduces an advanced image enhancement model that seamlessly integrates attention mechanisms within an autoencoder architecture. The model demonstrates superior performance in denoising and color preservation, out-performing established benchmarks. Leveraging a dynamic cross-attention mechanism, the proposed model excels in capturing fine details while mitigating noise, achieving a harmonious balance between denoising and color fidelity. The synthesis of a diverse dataset, encompassing both synthetic transformations and real-world variability, enhances the model's adaptability. This research contributes to the evolving landscape of image enhancement, offering promising implications for various applications in computer vision.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Spin-Coater for Thin Films Fabrication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper outlines the development of a low-cost Internet of Things (IoT)-based spin-coater for thin film deposition. Compared to existing commercial microcontroller-based spin-coaters, the standout feature of this spin-coater is its ability to connect with the user for system control and data input via hotspot/Wi-Fi/Bluetooth and to store data for future use. This spin-coater can be operated remotely inside a glovebox for device fabrication, providing superior monitoring of the spin-coating process through smartphones or web browsers. ZnO thin films have been deposited on a glass substrate using IoT-based and commercial spin-coaters. The structural, optical, and surface morphological properties of the ZnO films can be compared for both Systems. The experimental data shows comparable transmittance and absorbance, a 3.19 eV bandgap energy, and a 23.99 nm larger crystallite structure compared to a 3.18 eV bandgap energy of 21.68 nm in the commercial spincoater. The SEM images reveal a nanofiber structure. The system is simple, lightweight, and cost-effective, eliminating the need for a vacuum pump as required by commercial systems.

articleTitle: Detecting COVID-19 and Lung Diseases Utilizing Parallel CNN Model on Chest X-Rays Enhanced with GradCAM Visualization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The emergence of COVID-19 has underscored the urgency of accurate medical diagnosis, particularly in the context of chest X-ray image classification for various lung conditions, including COVID-19, normal cases, viral pneumonia, and lung opacity. In light of the pandemic's impact, there is a pressing need to develop resource-efficient solutions for automated classification, specifically tailored for resource-constrained devices. This article addresses this need by proposing a Lightweight Parallel CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) architecture capable of effectively categorizing the aforementioned multi-class cases. Leveraging a comprehensive dataset of 21165 images, our model achieves a decent accuracy of 93.21% for four-class classification. Notably, the proposed architecture maintains efficiency with fewer than 783k parameters, demonstrating its potential for deployment on devices with limited computational resources. This research contributes to the advancement of accessible and accurate medical diagnostics, catering to the demand for streamlined and reliable solutions amidst challenging circumstances.

articleTitle: GlioSeg 3D: Advancing Glioma Brain Tumor Classification & Segmentation with 3D MRI Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: One of the biggest problems in today's world is human health. The most important organ of the human body is the brain. However, many people overlook the well-being of this vital organ. Brain diseases like tumors or cancer often progress without noticeable symptoms until they reach a critical stage. Therefore, it's crucial for people to include regular brain check-ups as part of their health routine, just as they would for other organs. There are various problems or diseases are created in the brain; one of them is a brain glioma tumor. A glioma brain tumor is a type of malignant tumor that is highly cancerous and fast-growing. Its symptoms are not properly identified, so this tumor turns into cancer before people know it. Although there are different types of tumors in the human brain, one of the most common is the glioma tumor. The main objective of our work was to detect this tumor and create a 3D model for it. We have used different methods, like convolutional neural networks (CNNs), MobileNetV2, and MobileNetV3, and also worked with some machine learning models to find the most efficient solution. The CNN model was trained and tested on a dataset of brain MRI images, achieving a validation accuracy of 97.14%. Comparatively, the accuracy of the model using MobileNetV2 and MobileNetV3 was 97.80% and 82.20% respectively.

articleTitle: Exploring the Effectiveness of Transformer-Based Models and ML Algorithms for Bengali Hate Speech Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The number of internet users is growing every day. Social media is becoming more popular because the internet is accessible almost everywhere. People use social media to share their opinions and sometimes post offensive thoughts, known as hate speech, which can cause problems in society. There are many ways to detect hate speech in different languages, but there are few methods for Bengali comments and posts. In this study, we aim to identify various types of hate speech in Bengali social media posts and comments using transformer-based models. The transformer-based model 3cube-pune/bengali-bert achieved an accuracy of 75.99% and an f'1-score of 76.07%, which is higher than the other models we considered.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of a High Frequency Soft-Switching LCC Resonant DC-DC Converter for EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper suggests evaluating the effectiveness of high-frequency soft-switching in the LCC resonant DC-DC converter not only enhances overall efficiency but also minimizes switching losses, making it an ideal choice for improving the performance and reliability of power conversion systems in EV applications. This paper provides an overview of the fundamental operational principles, an in-depth examination, and the design of the converter parameters, using an exemplary case study as an illustration. This converter functions in two ways: a mode with a duty cycle of 50% and a mode with a constant frequency of 103 kHz. Operating curves determine the mode based on load demand. The study examined the efficiency of a power supply that operates within an input voltage range of 25V- 40V. It has a 48V output voltage and a 200W power output. We determine the converter's properties using the First Harmonic Approximation (FHA) approach and evaluate its performance at a steady state using PSIM simulation. We evaluate the simulation results of the 200-watt converter to validate the analysis, design, and showcase the converter's performance.

articleTitle: Predicting Football Match Results: An Analysis of Feature Selection and Machine Learning Techniques Using a Curated Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The global appeal of football is fueled by its exhilarating dynamic and unpredictable nature. Football match prediction is still a challenging issue due to its growing interest. The accurate prediction of football match outcomes has been a topic of significant interest for various stakeholders, including coaches, analysts, and fans. This study explored the use of dimensionality reduction methods and different machine learning models to predict the results of football matches. A historical dataset was created from La Liga matches spanning four seasons, incorporating both technical and tactical actions for each match and both teams, comprising 297 features per match. Most important attributes are chosen from the feature set using various feature selection techniques including Pearson Correlation, Spearman's Rank Correlation, ANOVA F Test, and Random Forest. For prediction, a variety of classification techniques including Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Naïve Bayes, Decision Tree, and Random Forest are used. The combination of the ANOVA F Test feature selection technique and the Random Forest classification method outperformed other models achieving an accuracy of 64.78% with 22 selected features when applied to an independent test set. This paper advances the field of match result prediction research by demonstrating how several machine learning classifiers and dimensionality reduction approaches can accurately predict the outcome of a football match. The suggested methodology can be expanded to other sports or high-dimensional data domains, and it has potential applications in sports analytics and team management.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and Image Processing Approach for Fish Freshness Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The proposed paper represents a new method for fish freshness detection based on deep learning and image processing. Our approach is an effective, accurate and Non-Invasive tool to classify fish quality using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Our model was trained on a diverse dataset that included images of fish at different levels of freshness. This CNN was highly accurate and reliable in distinguishing fresh from spoiled fish. The proposed approach uses convolutional neural networks and transfer learning with MobileNetV2 over ImageNet resulting in an impressive accuracy of nearly 97.50% on independent test data, better than the traditional approaches The proposed system is designed to overcome challenges encountered by conventional inspection techniques and introduces a fast, automatic in-line process for quality assurance. This paper helps decision- making in food safety and quality control of seafood, which is considered as a key advance for computerized fish freshness detection.

articleTitle: SHIFT-T: A Low-Cost Autonomous Mobile Robot for Trash Collection and Sorting for Effective Waste Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper presents SHIFT-T, a mobile robot designed to efficiently identify and categorize various types of waste for proper disposal. The robot classifies waste into three primary types: metal, plastic, and polythene. The system features an innovative trash classification and localization system that integrates within a mobile manipulator framework, enabling it to accurately grasp and sort items into appropriate recycling bins. This includes deep learning techniques, specifically employing YOLOv5 image segmentation neural network fine-tuned with a custom dataset for trash detection. An ultrasonic sonar sensor detects objects along the robot's path, while a camera module captures images and transmits them to a Raspberry Pi for classification and coordinate determination. This process allows for precise identification of an optimal grasp pose for retrieving trash from the ground. Finally, the identified items are placed at predetermined locations according to their waste categories as initially classified by the neural network. The model has achieved an accuracy rate of approximately 81 0/0, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying and classifying various waste items. The low-cost prototype demonstrates high accuracy in detecting various categories of trash and utilizes 6 degrees of freedom arm for manipulation.

articleTitle: Enhancing Email Safety: Harnessing ML, DL, and LLM Models for Spam Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In today's digital landscape, email remains vital for communication in both personal and professional realms, yet spam continues to compromise user privacy and productivity. This paper explores an advanced approach to enhancing email security by integrating machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and Large Language Models (LLMs). Our solution leverages ML algorithms, such as Logistic Regression and Support Vector Machines (SVM), to classify emails by analyzing content, headers, and sender details. To adapt to evolving spam tactics, we employ deep learning models like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to capture complex patterns in email data. The paper also investigates the novel application of LLMs, which offer innovative strategies for addressing spam beyond traditional heuristic methods. This paper attempts to train these models using a dataset comprising spam and ham emails. LLMs have swiftly reshaped the landscapes of business, consumer behavior, and academia, demonstrating transformational potential for society. Using a dataset of spam and ham emails, we demonstrate that this combined approach offers a robust and adaptable framework for improving email safety, illustrating the transformative potential of LLMs in enhancing spam detection.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Non-Linear Integral Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Controller for Stability Enhancement of DC-DC Boost Converter Using Fuel Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper proposes a nonlinear fast terminal control law that works on poor regulating voltage, chattering problem, transient instability and robustness with load fluctuation for DC-DC boost converter using proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC). In order to attaining the key features of nonlinear integral fast terminal sliding mode controller (NIFTSMC) a nonlinear sliding surface is designed that serves the objectives. To corroborate tracking of voltage, a mathematical model of boost converter and control law is formulated. Robustness of the controller with external noise and disturbance and load uncertainty is verified through the performance of proposed controller. Unknown parameters of dynamic model are predicted using adaptation law and stability and reachability of control law are ensured by laypunov function. Output voltage of proposed controller is compared with performance of other controllers. According to simulation output, NIFTSMC provides better response with regulated output voltage, small overshoot, less settling time, quick transient response and finite time convergence. It eliminates chattering problem and tracking error.

articleTitle: Safe-Women: an IoT-Enabled Smart Safeguarding Device for Enhancing Women's Security
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Women are expressing themselves as essential members of our society. But as the rate of women violence rises rapidly, women become less productive and embarrass society as a whole.In Bangladesh, women are not getting justice and this issue is now a great concern. Several smart solutions are available but the lack of effective features escalates violence against women. In this research, we have proposed a safety device using the Internet of Things(IoT) techniques to safeguard women from any kind of violence. This smart device can be carried by the user just like a wristband and the victim's location will continuously be tracked and the device will monitor her heart rate (BPM) and oxygen saturation ( <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{SPO}_2$</tex> ) continuously. In this situation, if abnormal BPM reading is found compared to the threshold value, an automatic alert will be sent to her guardian including a live video link. The guardian's Blynk application of their smartphone will display the victim's real-time location, as well as an alert call will be generated. Her guardian can also save necessary image footage. Our proposed system has achieved 90% accuracy after experimental analysis on twenty women which plays a crucial role to signify its efficiency. Thus our research implies that this smart wearable security device can be used to prevent women's violence ensuring their security all the time.

articleTitle: Mitigating Unbalance Due to EV Dispatch in a LV Distribution Grid Having Balanced Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The rapid rise of electric vehicles (EVs) in transportation is lessening carbon emissions and air pollution. Moreover, their integration with the electric power sector creates opportunities for grid operators such as improving voltage, reducing demand shortages, and addressing grid imbalance through vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology. V2G technology recommends that EV users dispatch their stored energy to the grid. This paper investigates the effect of uncoordinated dispatch of EVs despite balanced loads. Additionally, this paper will propose a new method to mitigate grid imbalance without requiring more energy support from EV users, a common practice. The proposed method re-sequences EVs among phases rather than reducing the discharging rate of EVs. This method has been implemented in a distribution grid, and the obtained results show that voltage imbalance reduces to below 2%. Additionally, the proposed method proves more effective than existing methods, benefiting both electric vehicle users and grid operators.

articleTitle: Broadband Graded Index 3dB Adiabatic Coupler for Photonic Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In this study, we present a novel graded index (GI) 3dB adiabatic directional coupler utilizing polymer material. Our design prioritizes both fabrication flexibility and superior performance. Through extensive numerical simulations and optimization using the R SoftCAD BPM, we demonstrate the broadband operation of our coupler across a wide spectral range. At the critical wavelength of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1.55}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex>, we observe low insertion loss of 0.10 dB for both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) modes, bending loss of 0.0017 dB, coupling loss of 0.02 dB for both TE and TM modes, and crosstalk levels of -31.10 dB and -30.16 dB for TM and TE modes, respectively. This device holds significant promise for high-speed optical interconnects in data centers, telecommunications networks, and integrated photonic systems.

articleTitle: Improving Efficiency and Controlling of a Pinwheel Type Horizontal Axis Wind Turbine for Low Wind Speed Area
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This interdisciplinary research integrates theoretical principles like Betz's law, Bernoulli's principle, and Navier-Stokes equations that helps in CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) simulations to design an efficient pinwheel type wind turbine. Through the use of CFD analysis, 7 different types of pinwheel blade designs are evaluated, and among them the most efficient one is chosen with an efficiency improvement of 51.4% over the previous one which performance coefficient was 49% for the given wind speed at 5ms<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> • The key engineering complexity involved designing a control system using an array of 8 hall-effect sensors at 45° intervals for 360° wind direction detection and blade orientation adjustment. Recognizing real-world challenges, a prototype is developed incorporating hall-effect sensors together with a magnetic pointer for dynamic blade positioning based on wind direction within the angle intervals that results in the maximum voltage and power outputs of approximately 4V and 2.66W respectively after testing. Despite having the lack of market constraints limits for the applicability of this research, this paper is aimed at surpassing the current power efficiency benchmarks and, therefore, becoming a prototype that remains valuable from the point of view of discovering new knowledge and innovations in methodology.

articleTitle: Optimizing MoTe2 Photovoltaic: A Simulation-Based Exploration of Sb2S3 HTL for Efficiency Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This work investigates the behavior of MoTe2 solar structure using the SCAPS-1D program and a Sb2S3 HTL material. The choice of MoTe2 is motivated by its high optical absorption, efficiency, affordability, and stable operation. The study compares a novel solar cell structure (FTO/CdS/MoTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) with a conventional baseline structure (FTO/CdS/MoTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). The new structure achieves notable advancements by examining various parameters, including HTL layer thickness, temperature, doping density, and surface recombination velocity. The device exhibits an efficiency of 40.33%, a voltage at an open circuit of 1.13 V, a current at short circuit of 40.78 mA/cm2, and a fill factor of 87.63%. The baseline structure features a Voc measuring 0.95 V, FF at 81.09%, J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</inf> at 38.15 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and efficiency at 29.35%. The integration of the Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> layer effectively lessens carrier recombination losses, indicating a promising pathway for achieving enhanced efficiency, affordable MoTe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based solar cells with Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> as the HTL.

articleTitle: Investigate the Performance of A Modified Automatic Sol-Gel System for the Fabrication of ZnO Thin Film
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This work's objective is to develop a cost-effective and modified automatic sol-gel system to deposit ZnO thin films with reduced mechanical vibration. The prepared ZnO thin films on bare glass substrates using modified automatic sol-gel and spin-coating systems have been compared and investigated. Optical characterization revealed approximately 80% transmittance within the visible spectrum and low absorbance, indicating high transparency and minimal light absorption. Optical band gaps were determined as 3.23 eV for the modified automatic sol-gel system and 3.22 eV for spin coating, indicating consistent performance. X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed well-aligned wurtzite structures in the films, with similar crystallite sizes of approximately 0.564 nm for sol-gel films and 0.5013 nm for spin-coated films. Overall, the modified automatic sol-gel system offers a cost-effective simplest system for producing high-quality ZnO thin films with good optical and structural properties compared with spin-coated ZnO films.

articleTitle: Development and Optimization of a Geometrically Simplified Microstrip Patch Antenna for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper presents a microstrip patch antenna intended for biomedical use, characterized by a simple structure. The patch antenna is effectively designed to resonate at frequencies typical of the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) bands, namely 2.45 GHz and 5.8 GHz. Notably, resonance is also achieved at 4.59 GHz, slightly outside the ISM range. Constructed with FR4 material, the antenna measures <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{48}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{48}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{1.6}\mathbf{mm}$</tex> and showcases a distinctive patch design. Performance evaluation reveals impressive return loss figures of approximately -36.87 dB, -30.08 dB, and -42.51 dB across frequency bands (2.39-2.49) GHz, (4.34-4.70) GHz, and (5.76-5.96) GHz respectively. Peak gain values at these resonant frequencies are measured at 2.54 dBi, 1.16 dBi, and 1.72 dBi. In consideration of biomedical applications, specific absorption rates (SAR) remain below 1.6 W/kg, with values recorded at 1.08 W/kg for 2.45 GHz and 0.96 W/kg for 5.8 GHz. Both simulation and experimental outcomes along with a comparison with the existing design affirm the antenna's suitability for biomedical applications, aligning with established safety standards.

articleTitle: DoA Estimation of Robust Hybrid Beamforming for Massive MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper presents an in-depth performance analysis of Robust Hybrid Beamforming (RHB) techniques in massive Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) system, emphasizing the integration of adaptive beamforming algorithms to enhance system performance. Focusing on Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR), Least Mean Squares (LMS), and Linear Constrained Minimum Variance (LCMV) methods, the study evaluates their effectiveness across various scenarios, including different user positions, antenna configurations, and environmental conditions. Through rigorous simulations, the paper demonstrates the superiority of the LMS algorithm in terms of beamwidth, directivity, and interference suppression under standard conditions. However, challenges arise in high-noise environments or when signal and interference directions coincide, prompting the introduction of a Regularized LMS (R-LMS) method to bolster signal direction resilience and maintain performance. Simulation and analytical results shows that the proposed R-LMS based Uniform Rectangular Array (URA) hybrid beamforming model outperforms in normal condition with Side Lobe Level (SLL) of ‐15 dB and Main Lobe Level (MLL) 0 dB. In noisy environment MLL reduced to ‐5 dB but SLL improves to ‐18 dB which provides better noise attenuation. The findings advocate for the potential of RHB in advancing beamforming technologies, promising significant improvements in wireless communication systems' efficiency and reliability.

articleTitle: Study on E-Mode AlGaN/GaN High-Electron Mobility Transistor with Composite P-GaN Cap and Recessed Gate Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study investigates a normally-off AlGaN/GaN High-Electron Mobility Transistor with P-GaN cap layer and recessed gate techniques incorporated in a composite structure. The hybrid structure significantly elevates the threshold voltage to 2.43 V and demonstrates excellent off-state properties with very low leakage current and power dissipation compared to individual P-GaN cap and recessed gate structure. An outstanding subthreshold swing of 34.12 mV/decade is achieved, and the breakdown voltage is increased to 1063 V. These findings demonstrate improved performance of the composite structure for high-power switching applications.

articleTitle: PCF-Based SPR Sensors' Air-Hole Attributed Performance Evaluation for Detection of Breast and Adrenal Gland Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Both normal and malignant cells in the human body are classified as intrinsic fluidic cells, and they all have different refractive indices (RIs). Refractometric surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensors using photonic crystal fiber (PCF) can be used to examine fluidic samples to help diagnose diseases. By comparing variations in resonance wavelength to the typical cell loss peak, these sensors may identify malignant cells. In order to identify breast and adrenal gland cancers, this study examines the numerical evaluation of four PCF-based SPR sensors. These four models, which were built with different air-hole dimensions, were examined for their sensitivity to RI. To strengthen the connection between the PCF and the gold layer, they have a Ti02 coating. Using the full-vector finite element approach, computational calculations were performed using the COMSOL Multiphysics program. Results show that within a limited range of 1.395 to 1.401, the sensors are effective in differentiating between MDA-MB-231, MCF-7, and PC-12, which are cell types that are associated with breast cancer and adrenal gland cancer. Four models (called ‘a’, ‘b’ ‘c’, and ‘d’) for the detection of breast cancer and adrenal gland cancer cells have computed wavelength sensitivities of 10,000 nm/RIU, 7142.857 nm/RIU, and 9285.714 nm/RIU, respectively. By comparison, the amplitude sensitivity that was estimated was -2658.02 RIU-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">I</sup>, −1599.52 RIU-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">I</sup>, and −843.181 RIU-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">I</sup>• Moreover, the model ‘c’ showed the most wavelength shift (140 nm) when compared to the models ‘a’, ‘b’, and ‘d’. The enhanced efficiency presents opportunities for enhanced non-invasive malignant cell identification skills in terms of early detection.

articleTitle: Hybrid Polymer-Based Integrated Beam Splitter for Optical Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In this study, we propose a hybrid polymer-based phase-tunable beam splitter designed to offer dynamic control over on-chip light distribution. Utilizing the transfer matrix method on this material combination, we optimize the device to accommodate changes in light phase ranging from -90° to +90° degrees. By introducing signals with varying phases at the input ports, we demonstrate the device's ability to dynamically adjust the splitting ratio, covering all possible ratios with minimal loss. With high tolerance, the device exhibits minimal insertion loss of 0.03 dB, bending loss of 0.007 dB, crosstalk of -27.5 dB, and coupling loss of 0.007 dB, making it suitable for demanding applications where signal fidelity is paramount.

articleTitle: Evolutionary Algorithm Based Approach to Reduce Total Harmonic Distortion for Symmetrical 7-Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In this research, some computational approaches based on biological evolutionary theory have been employed to diminish the total harmonic distortion (THD) of a cascaded 7-level -inverter system. Two evolutionary strategies, the GA (Genetic Algorithm) and PSO (Particle Swarm Optimization) are utilized to resolve the transcendental equations of SHE PWM for a 7-level symmetrical inverter voltage waveform. This study compares the lower-order harmonics and THD reduction performance of GA and PSO with another recent work of Bio-Inspired Intelligent Algorithm Based SHE in Multilevel Inverter. The THD values of that paper using GA and PSO were reduced in this research and also the individual 3rd, 5th, and 7th order harmonics have been reduced using GA and 3rd, 5th order harmonics have been reduced using PSO. This study depicts the use of evolutionary algorithms for SHE- PWM in multilevel inverters.

articleTitle: Development of a Low-Cost Alternative to AMBU Bag for Addressing Global Ventilator Shortage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Respiratory ailments like COPD and asthma strained healthcare systems globally, revealing critical shortages of ventilators as well as essential manual resuscitators, named AMBU bags, during emergencies, including the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak. Yet another significant issue is that the cost of traditional AMBU bags is beyond reach in underprivileged communities. So, the necessity for alternative solutions arose from the acute shortage of ventilators during the pandemic, exacerbating challenges for rural populations lacking immediate medical care. This study proposed a low-cost alternative prototype for AMBU bags, developed at a total cost range of 120 to 150 BDT, utilizing locally available materials to address this urgent need, particularly in rural and underserved areas. The prototype underwent rigorous tests like system parameter analysis, yielding moderate values within the recommended ranges from 1 to 42 cm H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O pressure that affirm its viability for emergency use. A thorough cost analysis is also presented to corroborate the affordability assertion by leveraging locally available materials, resulting in a costeffective and fully functional substitute to classic AMBU bags. However, limitations such as uncontrolled compression and expansion, and overpressure without fine-tuning capabilities, necessitate further research for advanced modifications. Nonetheless, this alternative strategy assures that critical respiratory support can be delivered during severe crises like pandemics, where traditional supply chains falter.

articleTitle: Dispersion Engineered All Normal Diffused Silicon Nitride Waveguide for Optical Frequency Comb Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: An Optical Frequency Comb has been numerically generated using a Silicon Nitride Waveguide. Geometrical parameters have been optimized for all normal dispersion profiles. Using a dual-wavelength pump around 1.55 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> in the all-dispersion 0.04 m long waveguide, a frequency comb spanning 88 nm with 10 dB bandwidth is obtained. As far as we know, this is the first instance such broadband frequency comb is reported in a channel waveguide generated in a single stage with small geometrical dimensions. This optical comb can be used in the advancement of optical atomic clocks, optical rulers, wavelength division multiplexing, and others.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Day Ahead Short-Term Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Electricity load forecasting is crucial for the efficient and economical operation of power systems. It involves predicting the future demand for electricity to optimize grid operations, manage energy resources effectively and ensure stability across the network. Accurate forecasting helps in mitigating risks associated with energy supply and demand imbalances and facilitates the transition towards smarter, more sustainable energy grids. Addressing the challenges of accurate forecasting amidst non-linear, non-stationary time-series data associated with electricity usage, this paper employed a hybrid deep learning model combining convolutional neural networks (CNN) and bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) networks. The objective of this study was to train the model to predict the aggregated active power demand on an hourly basis over a 24 hour period, using data from the preceding 24 hours. The model's performance was validated using historical power load data collected from the Power Grid Company of Bangladesh Limited. We compared four deep learning models to assess their forecasting efficiency. Our analysis revealed that the CNN Bi-LSTM algorithm was the most effective, achieving the lowest RMSE of 0.71493 and thus the least prediction error among the tested methods.

articleTitle: A Four Port Dual Band MIMO Antenna Loaded with SRR for 5G Sub-6 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: A four port dual band MIMO (Multiple-input Multiple-Output) antenna loaded with split ring resonator (SRR) is offered. The envisioned antenna will operate in dual mode at 4.8 GHz and 5.11 GHz; that is in 2 specific bands of sub-6 GHz namely the n79 band and LTE-46/LTE-U band. MIMO antenna elements' mutual interaction is reduced by positioning the opposite components in manner of opposition and assembling four elements perpendicularly to one another and finally achieved a standard ECC value below 0.5 and a good diversity gain between 9.95 to 10. So, the envisioned antenna for MIMO might be viewed as a possible competitor for sub 6 GHz 5G purposes.

articleTitle: Single Mode THz Waveguide Using Zeonex-Based Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study introduces a innovative hexagonal photonic crystal fiber (PCF) composed of Zeonex, aimed at minimizing confinement loss (CL) while ensuring a adequate level of effective material loss (EML) within the terahertz frequency range. The finite element method (FEM), using a perfectly matched layer (PML) boundary condition, is employed here to investigate the optimal characteristics of PCF. Simulation results exhibit that the PCF effectively transmits signals in a single-mode state. Remarkably low CL of 3.26 × 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>dB/m and EML of 0.1034 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> are achieved at 1 THz operating frequency. Additionally, the paper discusses other crucial parameters like core power fraction and birefringence. This cost-effective Zeonex-based terahertz fiber holds promise for diverse applications within the terahertz frequency spectrum.

articleTitle: Scrutinizing the Ion Migration Induced Performance Deterioration in Hole Transport Layer-Free $\text{CsSn}_{0.5}\text{Ge}_{0.5}\mathrm{I}_{3}$ Perovskite Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSC) have several potential benefits, making them a promising option for next-generation photovoltaics. Despite the efficiency gains, numerous challenges prevent this technology from being widely available. The most important one is that abnormal hysteresis in the J-V response may be caused by ion migration, which may be inherent and cannot be eliminated. This work theoretically analyzed the effects of ion migration in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{CsSn}_{\mathbf{0.5}} \mathbf{Ge}_{\mathbf{0.5}}\mathbf{I}_{\mathbf{3}}$</tex> PSC by using two defect models. The studied 1D defect models: (i) Model-1: defects at the bulk states/ defect traps, and (ii) Model-2: defects adjacent to the interface region/ interfacial defects; are simulated out in Poisson and drift-diffusion solver hosted by AC analysis (C-V, C-f (admittance), impedance) capable “SCAPS.” It is deduced from the studied models that ion migration leads to photocurrent hysteresis and can slightly but negatively impact the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{CsSn}_{\mathbf{0.5}} \mathbf{Ge}_{\mathbf{0.5}}\mathbf{I}_{\mathbf{3}}-\mathbf{based}$</tex> device performance and AC characteristics. On average, ~6.58% of efficiency is achievable for n-p structured (this work) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{CsSn}_{\mathbf{0.5}}\mathbf{Ge}_{\mathbf{0.5}}\mathbf{I}_{\mathbf{3}}$</tex> PSC, while the experimental efficiency recorded for n-i-p structure is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{7.11}\%$</tex>. This paper's findings are significant because they provide prediction ability to research performance deterioration pathways in noble perovskites, which is of broad interest.

articleTitle: Cancerous Skin Cell Detection Sensor Based on Multiband Terahertz Metamaterial Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The present study introduces a novel design and analysis of a sensor based on a metamaterial absorber (MMA) to identify cancerous skin cells. Computer Simulation Technology (CST) employs a finite integration (FIT) approach to simulate the suggested structure in the RF range of 4 THz to 7 THz. The crystal structure displays four distinct absorption peaks at resonance frequencies of 5.116 THz, 5.704 THz, 6.223 THz, and 6.646 THz, accompanied by absorption rates of 99.84%, 73.31%, 59.36%, and 99.77%, respectively. An investigation is performed on the absorption coefficients in different physical modes and the electric and magnetic field distribution patterns. The present study concludes by examining the sensor design and the identified mechanism. The maximum quality factor (QF), sensitivity (S), and figure of merit (FoM) of the sensor are measured to be 562.53, 3.9 THz/RIU, and 414 (1/RIU), respectively. Therefore, the sensor can be employed in biological applications such as identifying malignant skin cells.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis Between $\text {H}_{\infty}$ and Sliding Mode Controllers on Automatic Voltage Regulator System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study addresses the design of two robust controller types for automatic voltage regulators (AVRs): <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text {H}_{\infty}$</tex> and sliding mode controllers (SMC). Two AVR transfer function models were studied- the third-order model and the second-order approximate model. The AVR's performance criteria included rise time, settling time, overshoot percentage, and ITAE (Integral Time Absolute Error). A tan hyperbolic function was used to lessen the chattering effect in SMC. In terms of parametric uncertainties, SMC was found more robust than the H-infinity controller. The effect of injecting disturbance in the system was also studied. The entire design and simulation was done through the MATLAB Simulink software.

articleTitle: Developing Explainable Deep Learning Models for Android Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The Android operating system is becoming increasingly popular among mobile users due to its smooth handling and versatile features. But in recent years, Android malware has also increased due to its popularity. Cybercriminals deploy unwanted or dangerous software that might damage the device or steal personal data. Identifying and preventing malware threats in real-time is crucial to ensure security. In order to address this issue, we have created a framework that can continuously adjust to new mal ware threats while maintaining a high level of detection accuracy. We used a deep learning technique that can efficiently learn from both static and dynamic analytic character-istics of Android apps in order to accomplish this. Additionally, in order to determine which features are most relevant in identifying Android malware, we performed a feature importance analysis. This analysis gives security analysts and developers operative insights. Our experimental findings demonstrate that, with an accuracy of 95.87 %, our deep learning system performs better than several other methods.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient Self-Charging Smart Electric Bike
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Electric bikes offer a clean alternative to fossil fuel-powered vehicles, contributing to environmental preservation. This project aims to develop an electric bike with smart features including GPS live location tracking, smart display, and accident detection. Particularly beneficial for late-night commuters, the GPS feature ensures safety by automatically sending notifications for assistance when needed. The bike incorporates a self-charging system, reducing reliance on charging stations through a dynamo, motor, and battery closed-loop mechanism. Testing revealed the bike's capability to run for approximately 5.5 hours at speeds of 45 to 50 km/h without self-charging, extending to 6 hours with the self-charging enabled. The project also successfully tested the GPS live location tracking and accident detection system. This innovation presents a significant step towards sustainable and safer urban transportation.

articleTitle: Effect of Dye-Loading Time on the Performance of ZnO Based Dye Sensitized Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) represent a burgeoning photovoltaic technology with significant commercial promise due to their unique attributes, including semi-transparency, cost-effectiveness in manufacturing, simple fabrication methodologies, and strong performance in low-light conditions. The principal challenge facing DSSCs pertains to enhancing their efficiency and stability to bolster their viability as a sustainable energy solution. This research explores the impact of varying dye loading durations on the performance of ZnO-based dye-sensitized solar cells, which are fabricated on the FTO substrate. The study encompasses the analysis of I-V characteristics under both dark and illumination conditions, involving four distinct cells. During the cell fabrication process, the electrochemical Deposition (EPD) technique are employed for metal oxide deposition onto the electrode. A critical post-deposition step involved the application of hot compression at 60 MPa and room temperature to ensure the formation of a uniform, crack-free layer. Notably, the four sample cells underwent different dye immersion durations-30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, and 3 hours-as part of the fabrication process. Performance parameters under dark conditions were extracted using the principles of thermionic emission Theory. Additionally, series resistance and shunt resistance were calculated from the I-V data under illumination conditions utilizing the Lambert W function. Notably, the cell with a 1-hour dye-loading period demonstrated superior performance, achieving a 2.7% conversion efficiency, a short-circuit current density of 8.9 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{mA}/\text{cm}{}^{\text{2}}$</tex>, an open-circuit voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{oc})$</tex> of 0.53 V, and a fill factor (F F) of 0.56. These findings hold significant promise in advancing the efficiency of DSSCs as a sustainable energy solution.

articleTitle: Advanced Rice Leaf Disease Detection Using AgriRover: Enhancing Agricultural Monitoring and Crop Health Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Agriculture is pivotal for the economy of Bangladesh, providing livelihoods for the majority of its population and contributing significantly to its GDP. Rice stands out as the most significant crop among various agricultural products, yielding the highest volume of production in this country. A variety of diseases affecting rice crops can lead to reduced production, thereby impacting both the economy and demand. For this, early detection of these diseases can mitigate their detrimental effects on healthy crops and facilitate prompt pesticide application. This research involves the creation of a machine learning algorithm trained for identifying and categorizing healthy and diseased rice crops. Subsequently, the system is integrated into a rover that makes the system capable of traversing rugged land to assess the crops. A convolutional neural network known as DenseNet, comprising 201 layers, is introduced and leveraged as a pre-trained model for the classification of six categories of rice diseases. To ensure practicality and dependability in real-world scenarios, a rover is specifically engineered, enabling the deployment of the model. The rover is equipped to capture images of rice leaves and autonomously determine whether they are diseased or healthy, hence improving the overall detection and classification system of crops. The suggested approach represents a significant advancement in the holistic management of agricultural monitoring and crop health.

articleTitle: Detection of Malaria Parasite Using Lightweight CNN Architecture and Smart Android Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Malaria, a fatal disease, is brought about when a female anopheles mosquito bites. Death may occur from malaria if treatment is not received in its early stages. It is highly important to identify the malaria parasite as early as possible in order to proceed with the appropriate treatment. Thus, the paper proposes a Lightweight CNN model that is designed to detect malaria parasite by early stage from microscopic blood images. To reveal the usefulness of the proposed model, Grad-CAM was applied to detect the image part of most concern (which pixels draw more attention from the model related with the other pixels) by generating heatmap image. The Model's efficiency is calculated by accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Comparative analyses are conducted against well-known transfer-learning (TL) models and state-of-the-art (SOTA) models, with the proposed method. The proposed model yielded 99.56% accuracy, 99.97% precision, 98.36% recall, 99% f1-score and 99.2% AUC score. As, the proposed CNN model is lightweight the prediction time for a single image is about 2 milliseconds which making it highly efficient for practical applications and have significant impacts on healthcare accessibility, efficiency and even cost savings in the resource limited settings.

articleTitle: Development and Analysis of a Zeonex-Based PCF Chemical Sensor Working in the Terahertz Regime
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Photonic crystal fibre (PCF) has gained significant attention in recent years for its potential in terahertz spectrum sensing. By adjusting the structural parameter, one can control the optical characteristics of photonic crystal fibre. A hollow-core photonic crystal fibre was utilised to develop a low-loss terahertz sensor for chemical detection inside the terahertz frequency range in this research. The design we propose features air vents in the outer layer arranged in a hexagonal pattern, while the inner core consists of isosceles triangles and rectangles. An optical study of the design was undertaken using the full vectorial finite element technique (FEM) in combination with COMSOL multiphysics. The quantitative results of our proposed design have undergone substantial improvement. The simulation findings indicate that in the x-polarisation mode, the relative sensitivity for ethanol and benzene is 90.03% and 89.63%, respectively, at the optimal condition. Additionally, the simulation shows a low confinement loss of 2.12x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">–13</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> and a low eml of 0.026 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> This research also presents information on the physical characteristics and quantitative efficiency evaluation.

articleTitle: Deep Feature Fusion Based Brain Tumor Classification From Imbalance MRI Dataset Using Weighted Loss Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Deep learning using MRI images to classify brain tumours presents a significant challenge due to imbalanced training datasets, where one tumor type may have far more samples than others. The overrepresented class may perform worse in classifiers as a result of this imbalance. In order to tackle this issue, the paper examines how feature learning in CNNs is affected by weighted loss functions to manage data imbalance. The article propose deep feature fusion, where particular CNN model features that were trained using three distinct loss functions are fused and classified using softmax classifier. This approach lead to notable improvements in brain tumor classification compared to a CNN trained with standard cross-entropy loss. Notably, the proposed methods substantially reduce classification errors between uneven class samples. The proposed model achieved an impressive 94.5% classification accuracy, accompanied by an average Fl-score of 94.6%, average precision of 94.6 %, and average recall of 95%. These findings underscore the effectiveness of our methodology in improving brain tumor classification accuracy, offering a promising avenue for more reliable diagnosis and treatment planning in clinical settings,

articleTitle: Design and Development of Leo: An Affordable Biomechanically Inspired Quadruped Robot with Cognitive Abilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper presents the design, development, and testing of Leo, an affordable biomechanically inspired quadruped robot with cognitive abilities. The objective was to create an accessible, low-cost platform for robotics research and education. Leo features a lightweight 3D-printed structure weighing 2 kg, with dimensions of 550 mm x 400 mm x 100 mm. The robot employs a novel crankshaft mechanism in its leg design to reduce torque requirements and improve efficiency. Leo's control system integrates Robot Operating System (ROS) and Arduino, allowing for both manual and semi-autonomous operation. Cognitive abilities are demonstrated through voice recognition, image recognition, and object detection capabilities using YOLOv4 and face recognition algorithms. Gait analysis reveals an elliptical trajectory with each walking cycle lasting 19–20 seconds. Real-world testing showed a close correlation between planned and actual movements, with an approximate error of 25% due to practical conditions. Leo represents a significant step towards creating accessible quadruped robots for research, household use, and small-scale tasks, with potential applications in education, home assistance, and prototype testing for more advanced robotics systems.

articleTitle: Secure Wireless Communication Through Composite Rayleigh-Gamma Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper examines the secure performance of a composite Rayleigh-gamma fading channel when an eavesdropper is present in the channel. The aim of this work is to investigate the effect of gamma shadowing incorporating Rayleigh fading for the analysis of security in wireless communication networks in terms of probability of non-zero secrecy capacity (PNZSC) and secure outage probability (SOP). The analysis demonstrates that the shadowing effect substantially improves the security of the proposed model. Furthermore, Monte-Carlo simulations are carried out to confirm the accuracy of the theoretical findings.

articleTitle: Generation of Electricity Using Footstep Energy: An IoT-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In this paper, a non-conventional approach is taken into consideration to generate electrical energy just by stepping on the footsteps. By utilizing footstep energy, non-conventional energy transforms mechanical energy into electrical energy. The electrical energy can then be controlled or saved for later use. The goal is to maximize the energy that is being squandered while also obtaining a pollution-free energy source. A prototype module with a spring-loaded mechanical structure is built with the intention of producing energy anytime a force is applied to its surface in order to practically enhance this concept. Using footsteps to generate energy doesn't involve the use of fuel to produce electricity. With the aid of a rack and pinion arrangement, the proposed system is producing power. Although the production of power is highly valuable, there aren't many early cost-effective variables. This power source has numerous uses. It is connected to a microcontroller-based monitoring circuit, which lets the user check the voltage, current and power of battery and controlling the load. The concept of this paper is simple to use and reasonably priced. Installing this system is possible in places where people are always on the go, such as shopping malls, schools, colleges and any other crowded areas.

articleTitle: A Coastal Area Based Statistical Channel Modeling for 5G Millimeter Wave (mmWave) Heterogeneous Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Due to the vast spectrum and likelihood of widespread use in 5G usage, millimeter wave (mmWave) is recommended as a replacement for optical fiber for backhaul. However, human blockage and swift channel fluctuation brought on by user movement are the two key obstacles to mmWave communication adoption in the context of networks. Spatial consistency represents one of the least crucial factors in obtaining uniform channel fluctuations and assisting in the development of estimations of channels and beam tracking purposes. In a real-world setting for an urban macrocell (UMa) in coastal regions like Cox's Bazar, the largest sea beach in the world, this article explores the way human blockage and spatial consistency impact 73 GHz backhaul reliability for 5G mmWave-based networks. A thorough simulation of mmWave backhauling at 73 GHz has been conducted, and the results, e.g., power delay profile (PDP) and shadow fading (SF), will have a big impact on how complex heterogeneous networks of the future model their channels.

articleTitle: MultiClass Classification of Chest Diseases using CXR Images with DenseNet201+CNN and Grad CAM Visualization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Accurately identifying lung diseases is really important for treating them well, especially now with COVID-19 making respiratory problems worse worldwide. In response to the global impact, this paper has presented a deep learning framework for the multiclass classification of chest diseases, covering COVID-19, pulmonary fibrosis, tuberculosis, lung opacity, and normal cases. A modified DenseNet201 combined with a custom CNN has been introduced in this paper for a more effective classification of lung diseases. The proposed DenseNet201+CNN network surpasses key transfer learning models (ResNet50, VGG16, VGG19, DenseNet201) achieving a testing accuracy of 95.43%. This study employs DenseNet201 due to its superior feature extraction capabilities and efficiency in handling vanishing gradients. Contributions of this study include a 5-class classification system with a sizable combined dataset, addressing class imbalance through augmentation and rigorous model evaluation comparing with four other transfer learning models. The incorporation of Explainable AI (Artificial Intelligence), specifically Gradient Weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM), enhances data visualization, ensuring transparency in the model's decision-making process. This study strives to advance automated disease diagnosis, potentially transforming early detection approaches for critical lung conditions.

articleTitle: A Meander Line Microstrip Patch Antenna for Internet of Things (IoT) Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The paper introduces a design concept for a microstrip patch antenna operating within the 2.4 GHz ISM (Industrial, Scientific, and Medical) band, specifically suitable for applications within the world of the Internet of Things (IoT).
