The antenna features an inverse S shaped meander line connected with rectangular box, resulting in a compact size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{40}\times \mathbf{10}\times \mathbf{1.6}\ \mathbf{mm}^{\mathbf{3}}$</tex> and providing better impedance matching and efficiency than conventional meander line antenna. A parasitic patch and slotted partial ground are applied in this antenna. The parasitic patch affects greatly the bandwidth of antenna which is 20%. A FR-4 lossy material is used as substrate for this antenna. The proposed antenna has a gain of 1.14 dB, a voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) of 1.014 with 73.35% radiation efficiency at 2.4 GHz. Also, the value of reflection coefficient is -42.81 dB at 2.4 GHz indicating low power loss due to reflection. The proposed antenna is integrated with home automation system to verify its performance on IoT application.

articleTitle: Design, Modeling and Fabrication of a Symmetric Multilevel Inverter with Optimized Damping Resistor for the Solar Powered Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In this paper, a single-phase, 5-level symmetric, multilevel inverter is designed for solar powered renewable energy applications. This inverter topology is designed with only 5-IGBT switches which is comparatively lower switch counts to the other same level inverters. This study conducts a comprehensive examination of the multilevel carrier-based continuous pulse train with ideal modulation, employing the phase-shift position (POP) technique to ensure precise device switching. Moreover, the single-phase solar powered 5-level symmetric Multilevel Inverter (MLI) is designed, modelled and implemented with the appropriate filters where the damping resistor (rd) is optimized, and practically the FFT measured THD level is 6.33%. The LC and LCL filters are designed using the transfer function and checked the stability from the BODE diagram. In addition, the control algorithm for operating the switches of the designed and simulated inverter is implemented using the C programming language. This allows for embedding of the control section code directly into a Hardware-in-the-open loop (HIL) system.

articleTitle: Design of a Printed Planar Patch Antenna for Ultra-wideband Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel printed planar patch antenna design exhibiting remarkable performance for ultra-wideband (UWB) wireless communications. It offers a compact dimension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10\times 16\times 1.575\text{mm}^{3}$</tex> structured on Rogers RT5880 (lossy) substrate material with partial ground that provides a wider band ranging from 3.6 GHz-14.6 GHz. The operating region shows an acceptable flat gain where the peak value of the gain and directivity is 3.28 dBi and 3.96 dBi at 13.75 GHz and 14.6 GHz respectively. It exhibits an average radiation efficiency of 68 % which is satisfactory. The planar configuration proposed in this study allows for a compact and versatile design making it suitable for PCB technology with various UWB wireless applications.

articleTitle: A 9.14 μW, 66.67 MHz 4-Bit Bi-Directional Shift Register Using GDI-Based JK Flip Flop
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper undertakes a comprehensive comparative analysis of Serial-in-Parallel-out (SIPO) shift register design employing master-slave JK flip-flops constructed through three distinct techniques: Gate Diffusion Input (GDI), Transmission Gate, and Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS). Each technology's design process and key parameters are thoroughly investigated and compared, focusing on critical metrics such as propagation delay, power consumption, slew rate, frequency, and duty cycle. The proposed GDI-based master-slave flip-flop design has successfully shown 64.52% and 77.28% less power consumption than transmission gate and CMOS technology, respectively. The study extends its analysis by contrasting the performance of the SIPO shift register resulting in 22.58 ns and 4.552 nJ power-delay product. Results demonstrate the comparative advantages of offering valuable guidance for designers in selecting the most suitable approach for SIPO shift register implementations.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive X-Shaped SPR Biosensor for a Wide Range of Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel surface plasmon resonance (SPR) based X-shaped photonic crystal fiber (PCF) biosensor designed to achieve high sensitivity and a wide range of detection capabilities. The design and simulation were performed using the finite element method (FEM) with a perfectly matched layer boundary-based mode solver. Our results show that the suggested sensor can accurately detect analyte refractive indices (RI) in the range of 1.25 to 1.42. The sensor achieves a maximum wavelength sensitivity(WaS) of 29,000 nmJRIU and a resolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.72\times 10^{-6}\text{RIU}$</tex>, along with a maximum amplitude sensitivity(AmS) of 1581 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{RIU}^{-1}$</tex> and a highest figure of merit (FOM) of 558. These impressive sensitivities are the result of a carefully optimized design strategy, which involved selecting optimal geometric and material parameters. The sensor's high performance suggests its potential for use in detecting various biological samples, making it a valuable tool for medical diagnostics and environmental monitoring. However, practical implementation may face challenges such as fabrication precision and material compatibility, which are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Smart Billing Meter for Load Management and Tampering Alerts
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The main goal of this study is to present and assess the effectiveness of the proposed smart billing meter, evaluate its role in optimizing energy consumption, and validate its capabilities in load control, real-time data presentation, and tampering detection. This paper introduces a smart billing meter designed for efficient energy management. The proposed model incorporates essential sensors, an Arduino microcontroller with a real-time clock (RTC), and a vibration sensor for tampering detection. Integrating GSM technology ensures seamless communication between Arduino, consumers, and authorities. Simulation results showcase the robustness of the design, simulating load control during peak hours, real-time data display, and tampering alert mechanisms. The hardware implementation demonstrates effective load management, real-time data presentation, and secure communication. Safety measures, including validation checks and tampering alerts, underscore the system's commitment to consumer protection. The proposed smart billing meter is compared with existing studies to evaluate the novelty of this work which indicates this work is instrumental in optimizing energy consumption, providing real-time insights, and fortifying consumer safety.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Piezo-Electric Energy Harvester for Powering Cardiac Pacemaker
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper proposed the development of a bimorph L- shaped cantilever energy harvester intended for powering pacemakers. The primary aim is to propose an innovative method for pacemaker power supply through energy harvesting. The study emphasizes mathematical modeling, as well as the careful selection of optimal geometry and materials for the harvester. Various geometries such as V, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>, I, trigonometric, square, and cantilever, along with different piezoelectric materials, are investigated. Among the piezoelectric materials analyzed, PZT -5H and poled BaTi0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> are chosen as active components, with gold serving as the supportive material. Designs are subsequently crafted and simulated using COMSOL Multiphysics software. After assessing multiple designs, an L-shaped energy harvester with dimensions of 20mm length, 6mm width, and 0.3mm thickness is identified as optimal. The resonant frequencies are determined to be 41.25 Hz for PZT-5H and 44.17 Hz for BaTi0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, resulting in output voltages of 17V and 21V, and electric powers of 7.5mW and 11mW for PZT-5H and BaTi0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> respectively. The results obtained from COMSOL simulations are validated analytically. These findings contribute to prolonging battery life in pacemakers, thereby potentially eliminating the need for device replacement surgeries in patients.

articleTitle: Tailoring Visible-Infrared Light Absorption of $\beta-Ga_{2}O_{3}$ with Pyramid-Based Copper Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In this study, we have numerically enhanced the absorption of light spanning from the long-wavelength visible to the near-infrared region of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-Ga_{2}O_{3}$</tex>. Although <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-Ga_{2}O_{3}$</tex> is an ul-trawide bandgap material and typically absorbs only high-energy photons, we incorporated pyramid-shaped nanoparticles made of copper, effectively acting as a metasurface. Through optimization of the structure and its arrangement density, we achieved a 50 percent increase in light absorption in the wavelength range of 600 nm to 1000 nm. Notably, not only has the absorption been enhanced in the long-wavelength to near-infrared region, but also a slight improvement is observed in the range of 400 to 600 nm. The correlation between tuning the peak absorption wavelength and absorption band has also been explored. The final optimized geometry of the copper-based pyramid is a base span of 15 to 20 nm and a height of 15 nm. The optimized filling fraction is 40 to 50 percent.

articleTitle: Detection of Schizophrenia Using Attention Mechanism with Convolutional Neural Network on EEG Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Schizophrenia (SZ) is a challenging mental disorder, requiring accurate diagnosis for effective treatment. Early diagnosis of schizophrenia can facilitate a normal life for patients. Electroencephalogram (EEG) data contains valuable insights into brain network connectivity, enabling the detection of abnormalities associated with schizophrenia. Hence, this study proposes a methodology employing a deep learning-based model utilizing deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with an Attention mechanism to classify schizophrenia patients. In this research, each EEG signal undergoes decomposition with Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) to extract relevant features that capture the underlying neurophysiological characteristics of brain activity. These features are then utilized to distinguish schizophrenia patients from healthy individuals using the proposed method, which is evaluated on an EEG dataset comprising 45 schizophrenic patients and 39 healthy subjects. To provide a comparison, various deep learning models like ResNet-50, CNN and DenseNet Model are applied. The results indicate that the proposed model outperforms all other methods tested.

articleTitle: Exploring Optimal CsGeI3 Perovskite Performance and Investigating Suitable Hole Transport Layers for Solar Cell Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper provides a detailed analysis of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) with a CsGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> absorber layer, using SCAPS-1D simulation for evaluation. The study investigates the FTO/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/CsGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/HTL structure and explores several hole transport layers (HTLs) to enhance device performance. By optimizing the thickness and acceptor density of the absorber layer in combination with different HTLs, the research demonstrates significant improvements in efficiency. The use of Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O as an HTL resulted in an impressive power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 37.39%, exceeding the previous best of 35.91%. This investigation offers new insights into the role of HTL variations and absorber layer optimization, positioning CsGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based PSCs as a promising technology for future solar applications.

articleTitle: Refreshable Braille Display: A Review of Existing Technologies and a Proposed Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The world is currently undergoing the fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR), in which information plays a crucial role in everyday life. However, those with visual impairments are unable to access information by visual means. Approximately 237 million individuals worldwide suffer from vision impairment. The Refreshable Braille Display (RBD) is considered the most advanced and significant instructional tool for the visually impaired (VI), garnering interest from scientists and researchers worldwide. There are numerous technologies available to actuate the RBD. A comprehensive and meticulous examination of the existing technologies is necessary to make the proper choice of actuating technology in relevant applications. This paper aims to categorize the published articles based on the different types of actuation technologies that exist, and to examine each technology in terms of its benefits, drawbacks, and technical and economic parameters such as cost, power consumption, frequency, durability, etc. The analysis demonstrated that the electromagnetic actuation method is the most suitable approach from both an economic and technical standpoint. The authors proposed a RBD that utilizes the electromagnetic actuation approach. This method involves the use of a permanent magnet, electromagnet, and a cam in each braille pin. The proposed method is anticipated to fulfill all the necessary criteria and specifications of a braille display. The authors have already finished creating the computer-aided design (CAD) model of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Glaucoma from Cropped Fundus Images Using Transfer-Learned Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Glaucoma, a major contributor to irreversible blind-ness, which requires early diagnosis and appropriate treatment. In this work, we use deep learning techniques to automate the diagnosis of glaucoma from retinal fundus images. For increased efficiency, we use a cropped fundus images instead of analyzing entire fundus photos. We use VGG-19, ResNet-50, and EfficientNet B3 for binary classification on the ACRIMA dataset. Notably, ResNet-50 achieves 100% accuracy. Next, we combine glaucoma suspect samples from publicly accessible datasets with ACRIMA and DRISHTI-GS1 to create “Glaucoma suspect” class in a custom multiclass dataset. Using this dataset, EfficientNet-B3 and ResNet-50 produce 97% and 98% accuracy rates, respectively. Both models perform flawlessly when it comes to categorizing the suspect class & negative class with 100% sensitivity. Our results highlight the effectiveness of deep learning in glaucoma detection and provide interesting directions for enhancing diagnostic precision and facilitating early intervention.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Evaluation of Various Hybrid Energy Systems Optimization for Rural Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study presents a joint technical and economic analysis of hybrid energy solutions, emphasizing their practicality for rural Bangladesh. It promotes a comprehensive assessment to identify the most effective and sustainable energy systems for these regions. Bangladesh is currently facing energy challenges like load shedding and environmental concerns from reliance on fossil fuels. Thus, integrating renewable sources with fossil fuels offers a sustainable solution. The objective of this paper is to analyze energy demand, optimize system performance, evaluate economic feasibility, and assess designs for both off-grid and on-grid hybrid renewable energy systems using HOMER Pro software. This study specifically targets a remote area, Char Atra in Naria Upazila, Bangladesh. The key innovation of this research lies in its being the first to conduct an extensive techno-economic evaluation for Char Atra, emphasizing optimized resource use. The research analyzes three systems: two off-grid and one on-grid. The simulation results show that the minimum cost of energy is $0.187/kWh and $0.202/kWh for the off-grid systems, and $0.0647/kWh for the on-grid system. The renewable-only off-grid system has the highest excess electricity (24.4%) and the longest payback period (3.52 years). Conversely, the grid-tied system has the shortest payback period (3.2 years) and lowest excess electricity (0.24%). The sensitivity analysis evaluates the hybrid system's viability and resilience under various environmental conditions, renewable resource costs, availability, and fuel price changes. In addition to guiding future decisions on deploying hybrid systems, this research helps integrating sustainable and renewable energy sources in rural Bangladesh.

articleTitle: A Fusion-Based Approach to Multiclass Retinal Disease Classification: Transfer Learning Strategy with CBAM Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Eye diseases pose significant global public health challenges, often resulting to irreversible blindness if untreated. Early, precise diagnosis of these disorders is critical. In this paper, we address this crucial issue using transfer learning methods for the categorization of multiple eye disorders. The proposed architecture features a fusion-based technique that combines EfficientNetB0 and MobileNetV3Large convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for feature extraction and incorporates Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), which dynamically focuses on significant regions of the images, enhancing the model's discriminative capability. Our proposed model achieves outstanding performance on two separate datasets: 97.85% accuracy on the Eye Disease Classification (EDC) dataset and 91.96% on the Ocular Disease Intelligent Recognition (ODIR) dataset, surpassing existing state-of-the-art approaches in ocular disease classification. By developing the proposed model, we intend to contribute to the creation of more effective diagnostic tools and eventually enhance patient outcomes in ophthalmology.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning With Mutual Information for Selecting Bands in Hyperspectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Uyperspectral imaging (USI) is a critical technology in remote sensing that provides extensive spectral information for material identification and classification on Earth's surface. Despite its benefits, the high dimensionality of USI data introduces significant challenges, such as elevated computational costs and extensive storage needs due to band redundancy. This research proposes an innovative approach to hyperspectral band selection using Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) with Mutual Information as a reward mechanism, aiming to more effectively capture inter-band dependencies than traditional methods. This approach selects the most informative bands that provide significant contributions to achieving better classification results. The study also introduces an advanced classifier array incorporating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) alongside traditional machine learning classifiers like K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Support Vector Machines with Radial Basis Function (SVM-RBF) to leverage both spectral and spatial data relationships. The DRL model, framed as a Markov Decision Process, learns an action-value function to select optimal band combinations, enhancing classification accuracy and reducing data redundancy. Experiments conducted on the Indian Pines and Botswana datasets demonstrate that the Mutual Information-based DRL model significantly outperforms traditional entropy-based methods across all used classifiers, confirming the efficacy of the proposed approach. This integration of Mutual Information and a DRL framework offers promising advancements for efficient and effective hyperspectral imaging systems, setting a new benchmark in the field.

articleTitle: Idle Time-Slot Utilization for Latency and Energy Efficiency in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In wireless sensor networks (WSNs), sensor nodes are usually operated by low power battery, that's why energy efficiency is a main concern. Because energy efficient WSN provides longer lifetime of each sensor node. Several energy efficient medium access control (MAC) protocols for WSNs have been proposed to ensure longer network lifetime. However, to save energy the applied protocols may introduce extra end-to-end latency. In the conventional MAC protocols, time-slot is sequentially assigned to every node a in the time frame. Usually, the source nodes transmit data packets in their respective time-slots while the time-slots of the non-source nodes remain idle. So, the idle time-slots to non-source nodes introduces delay in gathering data packets and impedes time-slots utilization. To overcome such problems, this paper proposed a new MAC protocol called idle time-slot utilization MAC (ITU-MAC), where idle time-slots of the non-source nodes will be given to the next source-nodes sequentially. We have simulated the proposed ITU-MAC protocol to achieve results. The evaluated results show that the proposed ITU-MAC protocol provides lower end-to-end latency in each round around 15 to 55 msec for transmitting maximum of 10/20/30 bits data packets compared to the existing Energy Saving MAC (ES-MAC) protocol.

articleTitle: Implementation of an Affordable Gesture-Controlled Robotic Arm: Revolutionizing Patient Care with Precision
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Mechanical Arms can be employed as Collaborative Robots (Cobots) to carry out Pick and Place operations, Machine Parts Assembly in Industries, Material Removal, Precise Robotic Welding, Part Transfer and Machine Tending, Painting, various Medical Purposes, Military Applications like Bomb Defusing, Security Inspection and many other tasks. The goal of this study is to create a robotic arm that can be gesture controlled to mimic the motion of a human arm, using the Arduino, by selecting appropriate components, including the Arduino microcontroller, servo motors, and gesture recognition sensors such as flex sensors and gyroscopes. This study also highlights the programming aspect by outlining the development of Arduino code to interpret and analyze the sensor data and generate corresponding servo control commands. Finally, potential challenges and scopes for further development, such as refining gesture recognition accuracy and implementing more complex movements were addressed.

articleTitle: The Multipurpose Solar-Electric Tractor: A Sustainable Solution for Farmers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper introduces a ground-breaking project centred on the development and evaluation of a “Solar Electric Tractor for Multipurpose Agricultural Applications.” The tractor is designed to revolutionize traditional farming practices by integrating solar panels, a lithium-ion battery, and a dual-motor system. The solar panels harvest energy from the sun, providing a sustainable power source for both mobility and a range of farming tasks. The lithium-ion battery efficiently stores this energy, allowing for continuous operation even in low-light conditions. The dual-motor system serves dual purposes, propelling the tractor and facilitating various farming activities through a mechanical coupling mechanism. Field tests have demonstrated the tractor's efficiency, versatility, and reliability in performing tasks such as plowing, threshing, and irrigation. The economic feasibility and environmental impact of this innovation are also explored, highlighting its potential to contribute to sustainable agriculture. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the design, components, performance evaluation, and implications of the Solar Electric Tractor, offering insights into the future of eco-friendly and efficient farming practices.

articleTitle: A Circular Shaped SPR PCF Biosensor Based on External Sensing Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study introduces a circular shaped Photonic Crystal Fiber (PCF) employing Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) and featuring an open-channel arrangement, expanding its refractive index (RI) detection span from 1.34 to 1.44. Computational simulations employing the Finite Element Method (FEM) alongside perfectly matched layer (PML) boundary conditions elucidate the superior performance of the proposed SPR-PCF. Key metrics include a broad wavelength sensitivity of 27,000 nm/RIU, a notable amplitude sensitivity of 2944.94 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, and an impressive resolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{3.70}\times \mathbf{10}^{-\mathbf{06}}$</tex> RIU, underscoring its precision in biochemical sensing applications. Moreover, boasting a figure of merit (FOM) of 692 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, the SPR based PCF exhibits exceptional sensing capabilities. The incorporation of an open-channel architecture facilitates external sensing modalities, enhancing accessibility and affordability while ensuring a straightforward fabrication process.

articleTitle: Development and Optimization of CZTS-Based Perovskite Solar Cells with Novel TCO and HTL Materials Using Scaps 1D: A Comprehensive Study on Enhancing Photovoltaic Performance and Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Based on copper, zinc, and tin sulfide (CZTS), perovskite solar cells have garnered a lot of interest because they may be less expensive and more ecologically friendly than conventional silicon-based solar cells. In this work, we report on the development and optimization of novel transparent conducting oxide (TCO) and hole transport layer (HTL) materials for CZTS-based perovskite solar cells. In particular, we study the application of PEDOT:PSS as the HTL layer, PC71BM as the electron transport layer (ETL), and CZTS as the TCO layer with an absorber layer of CsFAMA. With device performance metrics like the maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 41.30%, fill factor (FF) of 84.99%, short-circuit current (Jsc) of 34.277406 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 1.4175V, this study highlights the remarkable efficiency and promising potential of the proposed solar cell technology for next-generation photovoltaic applications. These findings highlight the significant contribution of this technology to enhancing energy conversion and promoting sustainable energy solutions. Moreover, this simulation study serves as a valuable tool for guiding the development of perovskite solar cells, assisting in the informed selection of material parameters to achieve remarkable efficiency levels, surpassing previous models.

articleTitle: Two Stage Solar PV Generation using Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper introduces a Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control scheme to regulate a photovoltaic generation system's DC-DC boost converter and single-phase inverter under varying conditions. The proposed method addresses chattering, overshoot, and transient response issues in voltage regulation. Mathematical analyses evaluate its impact on settling time, overshoot, and noise reduction. Maximum Power Point Tracking control ensures efficient operation. Comparative analysis with conventional sliding mode and proportional-integral controllers demonstrates superior performance in transient response, overshoot, settling time, and noise rejection.

Author Keywords: two stage solar PV generation system

articleTitle: Improvement of Voltage Sensitivity of pH Sensor Based on Ion Sensitive Field Effect Transistor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Ion sensitive field effect transistor-based pH sensor is used for the measurement of pH in the vast domains of electrolytes. An ISFET works on the principle of changing current through the transistor in accordance with changes in the ion concentration for measuring the pH sensitivity of an electrolytic solution. The ion sheath accumulates charges, which causes a generation of voltage between the substrate of the ISFET and the oxide surfaces. The pH value of the electrolyte changes the concentration of OH- ion groups in the gate material. For the design of this model, Si is used as a base semiconductor material, and Al203 as an oxide layer, which works as a sensing membrane. It proposes a channel length of 2,..,m and an oxide thickness of 30nm as a design criterion that successfully exceeds the remaining sensitivity and achieves a sensitivity of 58.97 m V / pH. This research work also extensively shows the boundary conditions for oxide thickness and channel length, which give a correct criterion for ISFET model design. pH measurement plays a significant role in medical science, such as DNA pH measurement, and it also helps to detect the properties of bacteria and fungi, which are essentially important for diagnosis purposes in the food industry. It also helps in wastewater management, drinking water, and natural water sources.

articleTitle: Advancing Communication Systems: A Novel Low-Power ADC Design in 45nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper introduces a pioneering study aimed at advancing semiconductor technology, particularly in Analog to Digital Converters (ADCs), essential for modern communication systems. The research proposes a cutting-edge communication system leveraging 45nm CMOS technology, featuring an improved ADC with low power consumption. Addressing the critical balance between signal integrity and power efficiency in integrated circuits, the study conducts thorough theoretical research on ADC topology to devise a framework suitable for low-power applications. A key innovation is the introduction of a novel low-power ADC, showcasing impressive performance metrics including a 67 dB Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), a 62 dB Signal-to-Noise and Distortion Ratio (SNDR), and a 78 dB Spurious-Free Dynamic Range (SFDR). This work significantly advances communication system development and marks a milestone in the ever-evolving communication industry.

articleTitle: Classification of X-Ray Images for the Automated Severity Grading of Knee Osteoarthritis by Ensemble Learning Through EfficientNet Architectures with Grad-CAM Visualization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a degenerative form of arthritis in the knee joints commonly occurring in old-aged individuals which can cause extreme pain, deterioration of bone joints, joint membranes or ligaments, and irregularity in the knee joints. Being affected by KOA, individuals experience limited social interaction and diminished quality of life. The KOA can be assessed using the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading method. In this study, an ensemble model was developed to predict a KL grading reliably and precisely. Several EfficientNet architectures were implemented for the ensembling of this study. Among them, an ensemble of EfficientNetB0 and EfficientNetB4 pre-trained models gave satisfactory results compared to other deep learning or ensembling models. Here, the proposed model underwent evaluation utilizing the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) dataset which contains X-ray radiographs. The dataset was split into training, testing, and validation sets with percentages of 75%, 17%, and 8% respectively. The overall multiclass classification accuracy was 96.03% with an F1-score of 93%, specificity of 98.56%, and recall of 93%. The proposed model achieved an optimistic result compared to the transfer learning models and state-of-the-art models. Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mapping was also applied for the radiographs to implement Explainable AI for generating visual explanations for the predictions made by the deep learning networks which revealed the model's potential for grading the severity of KOA.

articleTitle: Robust Automatic Voltage Regulation Using Modified Super Twisting Sliding Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study proposed the modified super twisting sliding mode controller (Modified ST-SMC) for controlling the automatic voltage regulation (AVR) system and compared it with different existing sliding mode controllers. The particle swarm optimization (PSO) metaheuristic algorithm is used to optimize the controllers. Integral time absolute error (ITAE) is considered as the objective function of the algorithms. SMC performance is assessed with and without disturbance signals. Signum reaching law, power rate reaching law, and super twisting-based SMC showed inferior performance to the modified ST-SMC. It achieved the lowest rise time (0.0252 seconds), settling time (0.0717 seconds), and peak value (1.1333). Considering disturbance, the gain margin and phase margin of the modified ST controller-based SMC system are infinite and 39.8 degrees, which illustrates the system is stable under disturbance.

articleTitle: Identification of Shared Biomarkers in HCC and NSCLC: An Integrative Machine Learning and Bioinformatics Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are two prevalent malignancies associated with high morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite differences in organ origin and clinical presentation, there exist common molecular pathways that could potentially serve as therapeutic targets across these cancers. In this study, an integrative analysis was conducted to identify shared biomarkers between HCC and NSCLC. Initially, two microarray datasets were utilized to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in each cancer type. Subsequently, SVM was applied to identify SVM-DEGs within each dataset. By intersecting the SVM-DEGs from both datasets, 43 common SVM-DEGs were identified. To delineate the key genes within these shared SVM-DEGs, a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed using the STRING database, followed by comprehensive network analysis in Cytoscape. Through various network centrality measures, including MCC, MNC, and Degree, eight common hub genes were identified, namely TOP2A, CDK1, BUB1B, PBK, ZWINT, RRM2, NEK2, and BIRC5. The robustness and relevance of these hub genes were further validated using two independent test datasets, where their Area Under the Curve (AUC) scores from Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves were calculated. Additionally, their mRNA expression levels were evaluated in normal and tumor samples using Gene Expression Profiling Interactive Analysis (GEPIA), confirming their dysregulation in both cancer types. These hub genes could be potential biomarkers and lead to better treatments for both HCC and NSCLC, improving outcomes for patients with these aggressive cancers.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Lead-Free Novel RbSiF3-Based Perovskite Solar Cell Utilizing SCAPS-1D
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Halide-based perovskites show immense promise as efficient, affordable, and easily-fabricated flexible solar cells. But ensuring their long-term stability and establishing them as environmentally friendly, lead-free alternatives is still a real challenge. Therefore, in this work, Rubidium Silicon Fluoride <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{RbSiF}_{\mathbf{3}})-\mathbf{based}$</tex> Pb-free perovskite solar cells (PSCs) were numerically modeled and studied using the Solar Cell Capacitance Simulator (SCAPS-1D). Here, a novel cell architecture, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{ITO}/\mathbf{PCBM}/\mathbf{RbSiF}_{\mathbf{3}}/\mathbf{CuI}/\mathbf{Au}$</tex>, has been proposed, where a novel material, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{RbSiF}_{\mathbf{3}}$</tex>, is explored as an absorber layer with an optimum thickness of 800 nm. After analyzing and optimizing several parameters like thickness, bandgap, and metal work function of back contact, it was found that this PSC shows: 0.9140V as voltage at open circuit (Voc), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{23.70}\ \mathbf{mA}/\mathbf{cm}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> as short circuit current density (Jsc), 82.20% fill factor (FF), and 15.23% efficiency (PCE). Besides, to achieve higher efficiency from the proposed PSC structure, series resistance should be very small, but shunt resistance should be kept high, and an optimum temperature of 27°C has to be maintained.

articleTitle: Contingency Analysis of an IEEE 9 Bus System Considering Optimal Location of UPFC by Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Contingency analysis is essential for protecting the security of the power system. It is the examination of a power system when one or more of its components fails. A power system may experience contingencies as a result of internal component failures or as a result of external causes like equipment overload. Multiple issues, such as voltage instability, overloads, equipment damage, and power supply interruptions, can arise as a result of them. In power systems, a lot of Flexible Alternating Current Transmission System (FACTS) devices are used to minimize these issues. They are also used in the transmission of power to increase transfer capacity and lower transmission line losses. Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC) is a flexible FACTS device that can minimize active and reactive power loss and improve bus voltage separately or all at once; however, it is crucial to place the UPFC in the most advantageous position in the power system to achieve this functionality. In our work, analysis of contingency has been performed in an IEEE-9 bus system. Outages of generators, transformers, and transmission lines have been observed. Load flow analysis has been done before and after each outage. Based on performance index, the outage of each component has been ranked. The impact of each outage on the transmission lines is measured using another parameter called severity index. The most severe outages violate line MVA and bus voltage limits. Besides, to get the optimal location of the Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC), Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) Algorithm is proposed considering the most significant outages. The results show that placing UPFC devices in the bus system has reduced active power loss by 13%, and reactive power loss is reduced by 13.47 %. Besides real and reactive power minimization, the voltage profile is also improved after placing UPFC in the bus system.

articleTitle: Advanced Deep Learning Frameworks for Classification of Epileptic Seizure Using Preprocessed EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Detection of epileptic seizures has achieved significant performance by using various methods. Some traditional methods like Machine Learning (ML) exhibit satisfactory results but it has drawbacks of handcrafted features. In recent years, raw EEG data have been applied to various deep neural networks which give the advantage of automatic feature selection. In this paper, some advanced deep-learning architectures have been proposed with preprocessed EEG data. Experiments are conducted by the UCI-Bonn Dataset, employing five-class classifications. Raw EEG data has been transformed to FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) and it is input to three different models (1) Convolution Neural Networks fed with attention layer, (2) A cascaded of CNN (Convolutional Neural Network), attention and LSTM (Long Short Term Memory) layers are employed. Subsequently, the output of the attention layer has concatenated with fully connected layers, and (3) Three branches of CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) incorporating attention mechanisms are utilized, followed by the concatenation of their outputs. Later, layer normalization and dropout mechanisms have been applied at each layer. Finally, the results of these three different architectures have been compared and analyzed with previous related works.

articleTitle: Advancements in Radar Technology for Enhanced Adaptive Cruise Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In an interconnected world, radar technology plays a crucial role in enhancing vehicle safety through Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC), a system designed to maintain optimal speed and spacing between vehicles. This paper explores the integration of Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar with Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) clutter rejection to improve detection reliability in adverse weather conditions, specifically rain. The study involves a detailed simulation of an ACC scenario with multiple targets up to 200 meters away and moving targets as slow as 0.0083 meters per second, focusing on the impact of rain clutter on radar performance. The results demonstrate that incorporating CFAR significantly mitigates the effects of clutter, ensuring precise range and velocity measurements even in challenging environments. The findings underscore the potential of advanced radar technologies to enhance the robustness and safety of ACC systems, paving the way for more reliable autonomous driving solutions.

articleTitle: Microgrid Dynamics Control: GA-Optimized LQR vs. ILQR Controller Comparison
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study compares Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) and Integral Linear Quadratic Regulator (ILQR) controllers for dynamic power system stability. Using a Genetic Algorithm, we evaluate their response to step changes and impulse changes, focusing on steady-state error, overshoot, and rise time. The ILQR controller outperforms LQR with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0 \%$</tex> steadystate error, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.24 \%$</tex> overshoot, and a 0.01 s rise time, indicating its superior precision and stability.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Load Shedding Control System: Categorized Load Distribution and Management Based on Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The limitations of the antiquated power infrastructure combined with the rise of renewable energy call for a paradigm change in grid management. With the use of information and communication technologies (ICT), smart grids (SGs) can integrate distributed generation and self-heal to provide dynamic solutions. Microgrids (MGs) stand out as important players in this changing environment because they offer reliable, localized power solutions. To guarantee MG stability and reduce load-shedding it is important to optimize the voltage and frequency of the system. However, effective load management is required due to varying demand and resource constraints. The vital role that frequency relays play in this endeavor is examined in this paper. Frequency relays allow the intelligent use of classifying electrical loads into essential loads and non-essential loads based on frequency thresholds. This allows the prioritization of essential loads and the reduction of disruptions during periods of peak demand or resource constraints with lightweight infrastructure. In this research paper, the aim is to establish an isolated MG system that adjusts the categorized load concerning changes in frequency. As frequency changes based on the demand for fixed generation, this approach ensures a stable and uninterrupted power supply to all users and a proposed system for efficient use of excess power demand. To show how frequency relay-controlled load prioritization affects important performance metrics, such as cost, efficiency, and reliability, eventually resulting in less shedding and improved MG stability, practical consideration has been applied to this experiment.

articleTitle: Archimedes Optimization Based Proportional Resonant Control of Active Arc Suppression Device in a Resonant Grounded Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This research study aims to enhance the performance of the arc suppression device (ASD) in the resonant grounded distribution system (RGDS). To achieve this, in this research work, a voltage-controlled ASD is proposed using a physics-inspired Archimedes optimization algorithm (AOA) based proportional resonant (PR) controller. This robust optimization technique optimizes the gain of the PR controller at a rapid convergence speed and maintains a good trade-off between exploration and exploitation. The performance of the proposed AOA-optimized PR controller is thoroughly evaluated under various fault impedances and with the comparison of AOA-PI, particle swarm optimization (PSO) based proportional-integral (PI), and PR controllers. The proposed ASD with an AOA-optimized PR control scheme substantially reduces the fault voltage to 24.77 V, 24.82 V, and 26.20 V for the fault resistances of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{250}\ \Omega, \ \boldsymbol{16}\ k\Omega$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{26}\ k\Omega$</tex>, respectively. These results represent a significant improvement compared to the performance of the other controllers examined in this research as well as from the existing literature.

articleTitle: Accessibility and Inclusion: A Gesture-Based Human Interface Device for Individuals with Hand Impairments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a wearable gesture-based device designed to emulate mouse actions, thus enabling individuals with hand impairments to interact with and control a Windows PC. The device serves as an innovative solution to address the accessibility challenges faced by individuals who are unable to use conventional mice due to physical limitations. By leveraging the USB- HID specification, this technology establishes seamless communication between the wearable gesture device and the PC, enabling it to interact with a wide range of applications and services, including communication software and internet access for healthcare and food delivery. The study explores the integration of gesture recognition technology into the human-computer interaction paradigm, ultimately enhancing accessibility and empowering individuals with hand impairments to lead more independent and connected lives.

articleTitle: Secure Wireless Multicasting Over Duel-Branch Correlated Channels with MRC Diversity Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: A multicasting scenario over a correlated Nakagamim fading channel is explored in this paper, where a single antenna source transmits to a destination in the presence of an eavesdropper. The destination has multiple antennas, as does the eavesdropper. The transmission of the information is deemed safe if an eavesdropper cannot tap into it. In this context, the probability of non-zero secrecy multicast capacity (PNZSMC) and the secure outage probability for multicasting (SOPM) have been derived in closed-form based expressions which shed light on how different system parameters uniquely impact these metrics. The results show that secrecy performance worsens as the number of destinations, eavesdroppers, and the correlation coefficient increase, but improves with greater antenna diversity and fading.

articleTitle: A Highly Sensitive Dual-Core Dual-Open Channel Circular Lattice Based Plasmonic Sensor for Wide Range Refractive Index Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper involves the utilization of computational analysis to evaluate a sensor constructed from a dual-core-dual-open channel circular-lattice photonic crystal fiber (PCF). The sensor's performance is demonstrated through the finite element method (FEM) with a circular perfectly matched layer (PML) boundary condition. Gold is installed as the active plasmonic material, added externally to the fiber to streamline the production process. Instead of placing the analyte within the air holes, it is conveniently incorporated into the outermost polishing layer, offering a more practical fabrication method. The sensor exhibits impressive sensitivity along a peak wavelength sensitivity of 23,000 nm/RIU, indicating its ability to detect subtle changes in refractive index. Additionally, it boasts a remarkable maximum amplitude sensitivity of 2598 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{RIU}^{-1}$</tex>. The sensor's detection range spans from 1.33 to 1.43 RI, and the study delves into the impact of factors like the analyte layer, air-hole diameter, and plasmonic layer thickness on its performance. This enhanced surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor exhibits exceptional sensitivity and a broad detection range, positioning it as a highly promising candidate for detecting biochemical and biological analytes.

articleTitle: A Review of Grid-Connected Supercapacitor Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Exploring the Future of Renewable Energy Storage delves into how supercapacitors can be integrated into existing power grids as a sustainable energy storage solution. This paper specifically examines the use of supercapacitors in integrated with wind and solar power, two of the major renewable energy sources. Supercapacitors present a compelling alternative to conventional batteries because they provide quick response times, longer lifespans, and greater efficiency. These characteristics of supercapacitors are main reason to use them in situations i.e. fluctuations and intermittency of various sources of renewable energy. The paper begins by providing a comprehensive overview of supercapacitor technology, from fundamental concepts and design principles to their practical applications in grid-connected systems. By case studies and experimental results to illustrate their effectiveness in maintaining grid stability and supporting renewable energy integration, this report highlights the critical role that supercapacitors play in developing sustainable energy storage solutions for power grids. It also discusses future directions for research and development in this field, including emerging technologies and potential market growth. Ultimately, the paper discusses a more efficient way of energy storage and distribution using supercapacitor to make the renewable energy more efficient.

articleTitle: A Novel Reduced Component Five-Level Hybrid NPP Inverter with Double Boosting Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Multilevel inverters (MLIs) are highly popular for their ability to generate high-quality output voltage with reduced total harmonic distortion (THD). The integration of boosting capability into MLIs further enhances their performance by allowing voltage boosting, which is essential for applications like renewable energy systems and electric vehicles. This paper demonstrates a novel way of enhancing the voltage gain of a hybrid H-bridge multilevel inverter. By incorporating only one semiconductor switch across each dc-link capacitor, and carefully controlling it, the voltage boosting capability of a five-level conventional hybrid H-bridge Neutral Point Piloted (NPP) inverter can be enhanced by 200%. The dc-link capacitor voltages are balanced automatically throughout cycles of charging and discharging by employing appropriate switching states. No additional sensors or control hardware are therefore required. To enhance voltage quality, switching signals are generated using a low frequency-based optimum nearest level modulation (NLM) technique. The system requires a total of 7 switches with a Total Standing Voltage (TSV) rating of 11V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</inf>. A comprehensive simulation using MATLAB/Simulink is performed to validate the efficiency of the proposed topology. Moreover, outstanding dynamic performance is observed in a range of loading conditions.

articleTitle: The Design and Analysis of 5G mmWave Backhaul Communication Channels with Human Obstruction and Blockage Considerations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The exponential escalation in wireless data traffic, catalyzed by high-throughput applications, necessitates augmented bandwidth and superior service quality for forthcoming communication networks. This proliferation introduces a critical impediment: cost-effective backhauling. Pivotal 5G technologies, such as millimeter-wave (mmWave) and massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO), present a transformative research paradigm for delivering robust communication services. This inquiry delves into the intricacies of 5G mmWave channel modeling, particularly under conditions of obstructions and anthropogenic blockages. Utilizing the NYUSIM channel simulator, we meticulously scrutinize various channel parameters within a non-line-of-sight (NLOS) environment. Millimeter-wave technology, with its extensive spectral range (10–300 GHz), is increasingly recognized as a viable alternative to optical fiber for 5G backhaul solutions. Nevertheless, human obstructions constitute a predominant challenge. This research proffers a comprehensive mmWave channel model tailored to 5G backhaul scenarios, elucidating the ramifications of human interference on channel dynamics. Our findings reveal that anthropogenic blockage significantly exacerbates path loss and attenuates received power, thereby adversely affecting overall channel performance. By providing profound insights into the deleterious effects of human interference on mm Wave channels, this study contributes to the advancement of more accurate and reliable 5G communication systems, underscoring the imperative of accounting for human obstructions in future channel modeling endeavors.

articleTitle: A Cost-Effective Transformer Protection Scheme Through Microcontroller-Based Design Utilizing DFT Phasor Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper represents the design and implementation of a microcontroller-based complete transformer protection unit, utilizing a new DFT-based (Discrete Fourier Transform) current phasor estimation algorithm that offers a more suitable and cost-effective alternative to DSP-based systems for contemporary power systems. The conventional microcontroller-based numerical relay has limitations regarding malfunctions caused by decaying DC signals, magnetizing inrush current, over-excitation inrush current, and CT saturation. Since the developed microcontroller-based relay incorporates functions to eliminate these malfunctions, it has been tested and shown to be more reliable and sensitive to faults. The proposed single-unit relay is designed to provide comprehensive protection for power transformers, safeguarding against external faults such as overcurrent/earth faults, and internal faults through differential protection. Additionally, it monitors various transformer parameters including oil and winding temperature alarm and trip signals, gas levels, sudden pressure changes, and oil level, eliminating the need for multiple relays. The system is especially appropriate for small-scale power systems because of its simple implementation and cost-effective design. Testing on a commercially available relay test bench confirms the system's effectiveness in detecting and protecting the transformer from fault conditions.

Author Keywords: new DFT-based current phasor estimation algorithm

articleTitle: Bangla Counterfeit News Identification: Using the Power of BERT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Many individuals in today's digital age rely on the internet for news consumption. However, on occasion, these platforms distribute false information, which can have serious negative effects on both society and consumers. Fake news can be combated with tools, but most of them are only available to English speakers, which leaves millions of Bangla speakers out in the cold. This research highlights the potential of using an advanced transformer model and how to leverage YouTube as an easily accessible data warehouse to gather a diverse range of Bangla news content to enhance fake news detection for Bangla speakers. Our created dataset includes 1913 fake and 1995 authentic news titles, collected from fact-checking websites and YouTube. We evaluate several machine learning models for their ability to detect fake news using TF-IDF and BoW feature extraction techniques, as well as transformer models, including Bangla-bert-base and mBERT. Our best-performing model, Bangla-bert-base, achieved an accuracy of 84.19% and an F1 score of 85.03%.

articleTitle: SkinNet: A CNN Model for Improved Benign and Malignant Skin Lesion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Skin cancer poses a significant global health challenge, necessitating precise and efficient early detection methods. This study addresses the task of skin cancer detection and classification by employing a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. The model, comprising two variants named SkinNet1 and SkinNet2, aims to accurately categorize dermoscopy images into benign and melanoma classes, aiding in timely intervention. SkinNet1 and SkinNet2 feature custom architectures, with SkinNet1 relying solely on deep learning techniques and SkinNet2 combining deep learning with Support Vector Machine (SVM). By leveraging deep learning, both models extract intricate features from dermoscopy images, enhancing classification accuracy and facilitating the identification of crucial diagnostic markers. Strong performance is demonstrated through evaluation using an extensive dataset from the International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC) archive. In the validation set, both models achieve an overall accuracy of 88.5% and 90.5%, respectively, which improves in a distinct test set to 90.5% and 92%, highlighting the efficacy of SkinNet2 over SkinNet1. These findings underscore the models' proficiency in discerning subtle visual cues indicative of skin cancer. The convergence of deep learning and medical imaging holds promising potential for advancing healthcare diagnostics.

articleTitle: Optimised Clustering Association Rule Mining with Health Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Clustered Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) based approaches can be used to extract strong and higher-order asso-ciation rules. This paper illustrates the application of clustering to PSO-based association rule mining. This work investigates improvements to association rules and introduces an algorithm to perform PSO-Based association rule mining integrated with a clustering approach. The proposed algorithm does not require any user-defined threshold or parameters to extract the strongest rules. To measure the performance of the proposed algorithm, we used data on lung cancer and disease symptoms. The proposed algorithm shows promising results in terms of generating strong rules and reducing execution time from the experimental results and the comparison study. This research can be used to investigate the strong associations among diseases and related attributes. However, the application of the proposed method is not limited to the health and medical domain, and it can also be employed in other domains to extract associations among class levels and other attributes.

articleTitle: Designing a UWB Antenna at Receiving End for Wireless Capsule Endoscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Wireless endoscopic capsule systems incorporate the combination of hardware and software components to safeguard individual health. Among the various antenna technologies in the field, the Ultra-Wideband (UWB) frequency range is highly regarded for its ability to transmit medical images captured by capsules inside the digestive tract with high resolution and minimal signal loss. While passive capsules have been developed, the design of on-body antennas has lagged. This suggested study offers a comprehensive examination of a newly developed on-body antenna functioning within the 3.75-4.25 GHz frequency range. The evaluated antenna exhibits advantageous directivity, achieving 3.1016 dBi without a cavity and 7.9361 dBi with a cavity when directed towards the body. The intended placement of this on-body antenna is on the surface of the body. Simulations are performed with an abdominal multi-layer model, incorporating the navel region of a voxel model, to evaluate its effectiveness in various bodily contexts. The antenna's performance will also be evaluated in proximity to a human abdomen. The simulation findings demonstrate that the suggested antenna, whether featuring a cavity or not, enhances in-body communication when positioned on the belly, minimizing signal loss and exhibiting a markedly low SAR value. On-body measurements additionally validate the antenna's robust functionality. This tiny planar antenna is seen as a good candidate for integration with wireless capsule endoscopic devices on the body.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Highly Birefringent Low Loss Nested Hollow Core Anti Resonant Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper represents a high-performance hollow core anti-resonant fiber (HC-ARF) demonstrating exceptional potential for low-loss, single polarization high-power transmission applications. The fiber exhibits a polarization extinction ratio (PER) of 154 at 1.55 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> signifying minimal signal degradation due to polarization effects. Furthermore, it achieves expected low confinement loss of 0.06 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dB}/\mathrm{m}$</tex> at 1.55 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> with a broad bandwidth of 110 nm, enabling efficient light transmission. Additionally, it maintains a higher birefringence value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6.7\times 10^{-4}$</tex>, which remains consistently above <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 10^{-4}$</tex> across a broad bandwidth of 130 nm, indicating minimal polarization mode dispersion and ensuring excellent signal integrity. These combined key properties of this HC-ARF fiber enables the fiber for various applications demanding high-power transmission with minimal signal distortion, including high-power laser delivery, low-latency data transmission.

articleTitle: Household Energy Consumption Clustering Using ‘k-means' Algorithm: A Bangladesh Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Previous research emphasizes the need for effective power management techniques to optimize energy utilization and GHG emissions, and control peak demand. In Bangladesh, the residential sector accounts for half of the total energy consumption. Thus, understanding the power consumption behavior of residential customers to design effective demand-side management techniques is crucial. This study investigates the application of the k-means algorithm to analyze real-time household electricity consumption data in Bangladesh. The k-means algorithm, known for its simplicity and efficiency, is applied to a dataset collected from smart meters, revealing four distinct clusters representing low, moderate, low to moderate, and high consumption households. This clustering provides valuable insights for designing targeted demand-side management schemes such as tariff-based strategies. However, the study acknowledges limitations, such as a small dataset of 14 households and a single region, emphasizing the necessity for future research with larger datasets and regional variability to enhance the algorithm's effectiveness in policy-related decision-making for sustainable energy management in Bangladesh.

articleTitle: Dispersion-Engineered Silicon Carbide Channel Waveguide for Mid-Infrared Region Supercontinuum Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Supercontinuum generation in mid-infrared (mid-IR) regime is critical for major applications. This paper explores this phenomenon in Silicon Carbide based channel waveguide with Silica cladding. We numerically investigated a 1-cm-long channel waveguide using silicon carbide (SiC) as core material and Silica (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) for upper and lower claddings which demonstrated anomalous dispersion across a wide spectral range around the pump wavelength, resulting in supercontinuum generation in the mid-infrared regime. Using a pump source at 1550 nm for a pulse duration of 50 femtoseconds at 5KW input pulse power, a supercontinuum (SC) spanning from 0.91 to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{4.55}\ \mu \mathbf{m}$</tex> above -40 db spectral power has been generated. This is to the authors' knowledge, first exploration of silicon carbide as a guiding material in channel waveguide.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning Based Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation Classification Using Continuous Wavelet Transform Scalogram
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common cardiac arrhythmia, is linked to comorbidity, heart failure, and aging. Its erratic and intermittent behavior makes reliable detection difficult. Recent research has demonstrated the usefulness of nonlinear time and frequency domain characteristics in the detection of AF through the application of deep learning (DL) and other machine learning (ML) techniques. In this study, the CPSC 2021 dataset was used to create continuous wavelet transform (CWT)-based scalogram images from cardiac rhythms comprising normal, persistent atrial fibrillation (PAF), and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (PoxyAF). The challenge involved classifying normal and PAF scalogram images, as well as three classes of classification: normal, PAF, and PoxyAF, for which transfer learning (TL) models were utilized. A number of TL models were trained; among them, EfficientNetB7 obtained a testing accuracy of 99.27% for two-class classification, whereas MobileNet achieved 93.23% for three-class classification.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of 4-Bit Adder Architectures for Enhanced Efficiency in Conventional CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Throughout the years, with the miniaturization of VLSI technology, adders form an essential component of almost every contemporary integrated circuit. The prerequisite of an adder is that it is primarily fast and secondarily efficient in terms of power consumption and chip area. The race to create the most optimized device structure is getting harder and faster, as more compact digital devices with the lowest power consumption keep coming out and replacing each other. The optimal adder architecture is crucial for modern digital systems to enhance performance. Hence, choosing a perfect architecture that is compact and has low power consumption can be done with conventional CMOS technology by rationally comparing the different types of adders based on various performance parameters. Among the vast realm of adders, this research paper analyzes five 4-bit adder architectures, namely Ripple Carry Adder (RCA), Carry Look Ahead Adder (CLA), Carry Select Adder (CSA), Carry Save Adder (CSaA), and lastly Carry Skip Adder (CSkA). The study evaluates performance metrics of adder architectures including transistor count, average power, area, frequency, and propagation delay using Cadence Virtuoso. This work shows that RCA has simplicity but a significant propagation delay. On the other hand, the CLA improves speed but uses increased area. Innovative carry-save techniques can help to mitigate delay. Considering all parameters, CSkA is the most efficient adder with the least transistor count of 182, area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{16880}\ \mu m^{2}$</tex>, and average power requirement of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{50.04}\ \mu \mathbf{Watt}$</tex>.

articleTitle: TomatoLDP-Net: A Light-Weight Convolutional Neural Network for Revolutionizing Tomato Leaf Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In addressing the critical challenge of plant disease detection in agriculture, particularly within African and Asian regions, this study introduces TomatoLDP-Net, a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) optimized for the precise identification of tomato leaf diseases. With global tomato production exceeding 180 million metric tons, disease vulnerability poses a significant threat to both economic stability and food security. Traditional detection methods, often manual and error-prone, are increasingly inadequate. Utilizing artificial intelligence (AI), specifically deep learning (DL) techniques, TomatoLDP-Net leverages a multi-column CNN architecture with varied filter sizes (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\times 3,\ 5\times 5$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7\times 7$</tex>) to effectively capture the diverse range of disease symptoms across scales. This approach, enhanced by dropout layers and softmax-averaging for prediction, showcases superior accuracy and reliability over conventional models, significantly improving disease classification with an impressive accuracy rate of 99.69%. TomatoLDP-Net not only marks a significant advancement in precision agriculture but also plays a pivotal role in ensuring the sustainability of tomato production and bolstering global food security, thereby addressing key agricultural challenges with cutting-edge AI technology.

articleTitle: Advancements in Nanostructure Engineering: A Wheel-Shaped High-Sensitivity Surface Plasmon Resonance Refractive Index Sensor for Enhanced Analyte Detection and Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study performed an extensive investigation into the performance exploration of Photonic Crystal Fiber refractive index sensors based on Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR-PCF). Numerical investigation of the sensor's properties was performed using the Finite Element Method (FEM) in COMSOL Multiphysics software. Thin coatings of titanium dioxide (TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and gold (Au) enhanced sensor performance by acting as plasmonic materials around the PCF. The proposed sensor detected unknown layer of analytes along the refractive index (RI) that ranges from 1.33 to 1.42. After optimization of different parameters, the proposed PCF-SPR sensor showed an outstanding performance by achieving a maximum Amplitude Sensitivity (AS) of 1998.9892 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. Also, a highest wavelength sensitivity (WS) of 25,000 nm/ RIU, and a notable figure of merit (FOM) of 531.915 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, demonstrated its accuracy and effectiveness. This design exhibited a favorable sensing performance by achieving higher wavelength sensitivity, better sensor resolution, and simplicity of fabrication. Furthermore, the proposed sensor will be significant in scientific, biological, and industrial domains and may be used for multi-sensing applications like temperature sensing, magnetic field detecting, etc.

articleTitle: Analysis of Kinematic Features of Handwriting Data to Detect Parkinson's Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Across various neurodegenerative diseases, the second most common disease is Parkinson's disease. It affects the brain cells, which are accountable for releasing dopamine. When there is less release of dopamine, the muscles of the body can't work properly, which creates a problem for a person. In recent years, it caught the eyes of researchers that handwriting analysis can be a good solution to identify Parkinson's disease. Various attempts have already been made since the discovery of this idea. In this work, we have tried to use kinematic features of handwriting to detect Parkinson's disease. As there was less data variational autoencoder was used to generate synthetic data to train the model and the obtained accuracy of this proposed model is 89%

articleTitle: High Frequency Control Logic Design for Asymmetrical Input CHB Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This work reports twelve switches cascaded H bridge (CHB) multilevel inverters (MLI) for asymmetrical input sources and high frequency control strategies.
