The proposed inverter consists of only twelve switches and is able to generate up to 27 level through asymmetrical switching as well as high frequency-based multi-carrier pulse width modulation (MCPWM) techniques. All the expressions for the switch logic to generate 7 level to 27 level are provided in the methodology sections and a few simulation results are plotted for the realization of the control techniques. As the proposed inverter is capable to generate higher levels with the suggested control strategy, the topology will automatically be claimed as a reduced switch and component count structure. The total harmonic distortion (THD) is improved in the output as the number of levels is getting increases.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of a Compact Two-Port Circularly Polarized MIMO Antenna for Sub-6 GHz 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This research presents the design of a compact, dual-port, circularly polarized (CP) multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna operating within the sub-6 GHz band designated for 5G cellular networks. This design emphasizes achieving smaller dimensions while preserving the functionalities of circularly polarized (CP) radiation and multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) technology. Utilizing a single radiating slot fed by an elliptical ring slot, the single antenna achieves circular polarization between 3.67 GHz and 3.81 GHz. The proposed MIMO antenna provides an impedance bandwidth of 340 MHz (reflection coefficient ≤,-10 dB) spanning from 3.57 GHz to 3.91 GHz and a 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth ranging from 3.65 GHz to 3.76 GHz. This configuration effectively covers the prospective 5G band with right-handed circular polarization. The performance of the MIMO antenna was validated through the evaluation of key metrics like the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) and diversity gain (DG). The results demonstrate a low ECC value (ECC < 0.001), indicating minimal signal correlation between antenna ports. Additionally, the measured antenna isolation exceeds −20 dB, signifying sufficient decoupling between the ports. These findings confirm the antenna's suitability for MIMO applications by satisfying the established requirements for low correlation and adequate isolation in a MIMO environment.

articleTitle: Maximizing Sb2Se3 Thin Film Solar Cell Performance: Optimization of Efficiency and Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, a mineral abundantly available on Earth, has emerged as a potential candidate for next-generation photovoltaic technologies. Thin-film Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> solar cells have garnered significant attention for their ability to utilize widely accessible resources, offering a sustainable pathway for energy production. This research focuses on the influence of crucial factors such as operating temperature, minority carrier lifetime, and defect density on the stability and performance of FTO/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/PTAA solar cells. When operated at an optimal temperature of 300K, with a minority carrier lifetime of 1000 ns and a defect density of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1}\mathbf{E}\mathbf{14}\ \mathbf{cm}^{-3}$</tex>, he device achieved a peak efficiency of 34.14%. Furthermore, the device exhibited an impressive fill factor of 87.96%, a Voc of 0.994V and a jsc of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{39.00}\ \mathbf{mA}/\mathbf{cm}^{2}$</tex>. These findings underscore the promising role of Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin films in advancing renewable energy solutions by optimizing material properties for enhanced efficiency and stability in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Innovative Design and Optimization of a Highly Sensitive PCF-Based Surface Plasmon Resonance Refractive Index Sensor for Enhanced Analyte Detection and Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study presents a numerical simulation that analyses the functionality of plasmonic material sensor elements combined with a photonic crystal fiber (PCF) using the finite element method (FEM). A simple geometric framework is used to assemble the portions of silica and gold (Au) with a 50 nm gold thickness, in the sensor. Our suggested sensor component performs exceptionally well, differentiating it apart from earlier research on amplitude-sensitive (AS) and wavelength-sensitive (WS) evaluating methods. The range of the sensor component's refractive index (RI) is 1.35 to 1.39 RIU. Based on obtained numerical results, the greatest sensitivity for amplitude and spectral interrogation methods are stated to be -422 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> and 10,000 nm/RIU, respectively. This approach offers an impressive resolution of 1x10–5 RIU for y-polarized measurements in terms of sensor resolution.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Bilayer Perovskite Solar Cells: Evaluating MASnI3/CsGeI3 and CH3NH3SnBr3/CsGeI3 Structures for Enhanced Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study examines CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/CsGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and MASnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/CsGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> configurations using TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as the electron transport layer (ETL) and Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O as the hole transport layer (HTL). Key parameters such as doping concentration and minority carrier lifetime were optimized using SCAPS-1D. Under optimal conditions, CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/CsGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> structures achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.5%, while MASnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/CsGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> structures reached a PCE of 22.48%. These results highlight the potential of these bilayer structures for efficient lead-free perovskite solar cells, promoting clean and sustainable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Data Driven Air Quality Analysis and Predictions: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Air is one of the natural elements of the world. Due to the growth of civilization and industries the air around us has become more polluted. So, predicting the air quality has become a necessary step. By predicting the air quality beforehand, we can take the necessary steps to make the place and the people aware. Machine learning algorithms can help to detect air quality using air pollutants elements. Many research has been done in this field so there are datasets that are available which we can use to predict the air quality. Accurate air quality forecasts can enable timely interventions and raise public awareness. In this study, we utilize machine learning algorithms to predict air quality based on air pollutant PM2.5 from 2016 to 2023. We employed five machine learning models: K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) Classifier, Random Forest, Gaussian Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Logistic Regression. Our findings indicate that KNN classifier performed the best among the models. This provides valuable insights into the effectiveness of different machine learning approaches for air quality prediction.

Author Keywords: Support Vector Machine and Logistic Regression

articleTitle: Feasibility Assessment of an Off-grid Hybrid Energy System for a Char Area in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper presents a thorough investigation into the deployment of an off-grid hybrid energy system (HES) in Urirchar, Bangladesh, aimed at alleviating the persistent energy challenges in this remote island community. The system integrates solar, wind, and battery storage technologies to suit Urirchar's unique geographical and environmental context. HOMER PRO software has been utilized for techno-economic and environmental assessments, considering factors such as initial investment, operational costs, and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> reduction. Additionally, MATLAB was utilized to demonstrate performance analysis. The HOMER output reveals a cost of energy at 0.395 USD/kWh and a net present cost of 1.86 million USD. The findings highlight the potential of the off-grid HES to adopt energy access in Urirchar, thereby fostering socioeconomic development and enhancing residents' quality of life. This research serves as a valuable resource for policymakers, energy planners, and stakeholders grappling with similar energy challenges in remote regions, offering insights into viable and sustainable solutions.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Multiple Sensors Based Affordable Autonomous Firefighting Robot for Fire Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In critical fire scenarios, experienced firefighters face significant risks that could be mitigated by employing fully autonomous firefighting robots equipped with multiple sensors. Our paper introduces such a robot, which utilizes flame sensors to detect fires and a pump with a water supply to extinguish them, an ultrasonic sensor enables obstacle avoidance during movement, while a gas sensor and buzzer provide alerts for gas leaks. The robot's mobility is ensured by wheel-attached gear motors connected through a motor driver, with all functionalities simultaneously controlled by an Arduino UNO R3 microcon-troller board. A key challenge was maintaining the overall cost of the basic prototype as low as possible, at approximately 25 USD. Our results demonstrate that the microcontroller board efficiently manages all these functionalities, swiftly detecting and extinguishing fires within the test environment, even in the presence of obstacles. The system detects fires within an average of 3 seconds and extinguishes them within 0–15 seconds, depending on the flame size. It also exhibits obstacle detection and avoidance capabilities with an average accuracy of 80–90 % in the test environment, ensuring precise navigation to the fire source and unobstructed fire suppression. Additionally, it promptly identifies gas leaks and activates the alarm system, outperforming many existing robots at this scale.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Ensemble Methods for Short-Term Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Forecasting electricity load is essential to the effective administration and functioning of power systems. This paper investigates the efficacy of various ensemble methods in Short-Term Load Forecasting (STLF) using a real-world dataset. We explore the implementation and comparative performance of four advanced ensemble models: Random Forest (RF) with Extra Trees Regressor (ETR), RF with XGBoost (XGB), XGB with ETR, and a Voting Regressor combining all aforementioned models. Our study focuses on developing these models, preprocessing data, and meticulously tuning parameters to optimize forecasting accuracy and robustness. The models are evaluated using different precision matrices such as R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). The Voting Regressor model exhibited the best performance in this work, as indicated by their low RMSE and MAE values and high R2 scores.

articleTitle: Enhancing DC-Bus Voltage Stability in DC Distribution Networks with Constant Power Loads Using Modified Integral Sliding Mode Controllers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In DC distribution networks (DCDNs), the integration of constant power loads (CPLs) with the DC bus can result in voltage fluctuations or system instability due to their negative damping characteristics. This paper introduces an innovative solution by implementing an integral sliding mode controller coupled with a modified reaching law. Initially, the dynamical model of DC-DC converters (DDBCs) operating with CPLs is developed. The proposed controller is then carefully designed to ensure system stability, leveraging the Lyapunov stability theory. To validate the controller's effectiveness, extensive simulations are conducted using MATLAB/Simulink, focusing on supply voltage and voltage fluctuations of the DC bus. The controller's performance is rigorously evaluated and compared with an existing controller, highlighting its superior capabilities. Simulation results demonstrate the enhanced performance of the proposed controller through various quantitative metrics, confirming its effectiveness in managing voltage fluctuations and maintaining system stability in DCDNs.

articleTitle: Enhanced Mitochondrial Segmentation with Customized Attention U-Net and Nakagami Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Accurate and efficient segmentation of mitochondria from electron microscopy images is crucial for a wide range of biological and medical applications. In this paper, we present a novel approach to improve mitochondrial segmentation by introducing an added Nakagami parametric (ANP) image-based preprocessing technique. We combine this preprocessed image with the original input that enhances the robustness and generalization of the segmentation model. To find the optimal combination of methods, we explore three different loss functions to train our model for varying epochs. We adopt the Attention U-Net architecture, customized it according to our strategy and demonstrated its superior performance in terms of mean Intersection over Union (IoU) and mean Dice score when compared to state-of-the-art methods. Our results showcase the potential of our approach for improved mitochondrial segmentation, offering significant contributions to biomedical image analysis and related fields.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Solid-state Dye Sensitized Solar Cell with Sb2S3 as Novel Hole Transport Material
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Solid-state dye-sensitized solar cell (ss-DSSC) has drawn the recent contemplation of photovoltaic (PV) fraternity as a viable substitute for fluid electrolyte for improving power generation efficiency, durability and minimizing instability in dye-sensitive solar cells. Nevertheless, ss-DSSC suffers from poor performance, which can be improved by including a hole transport layer. This work presents device modelling of a Al/FTO/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Z907/Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Ni ss-DSSC with antimony trisulphide (Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) as a novel hole conductor. The PV characteristics of the ss-DSSC covering the influence of charge transport layer (Electron and hole transport layers) thicknesses, doping concentration together with defect density of hole transport material (HTM), and ambient temperature are evaluated by means of the SCAPS-1D software package. The estimated results provide PV performance parameters with voltage in open circuit (VOC) of 1.28 V, current density in short circuit (JSC) of 15.97 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, fill factor (FF) of 84.15% and efficiency of 17.23% in proposed structure, highlighting the potential of Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>as HTM. Consequently, these results might offer a valuable perspective for creating innovative, affordable, and extremely effective ss-DSSCs.

articleTitle: Optimizing Rooftop Solar PV Systems for Energy Efficiency in Urban Environments: A Case Study of Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study investigates the optimization of rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) systems to enhance energy efficiency in urban environments, focusing on a case study in Bangladesh. Amid rising global energy consumption and environmental concerns, rooftop solar PV systems offer a sustainable alternative to energy generation. Despite the substantial initial investment, these systems provide long-term cost savings due to low operational and maintenance expenses. This research addresses challenges in efficiently utilizing the roof areas of academic buildings for solar installations, considering factors such as shading, tilt angle, and geographical location. The study reveals significant energy generation and cost reduction potential, with rooftop solar installations capable of decreasing grid energy consumption and fostering sustainable development. Findings emphasize the importance of optimal design and implementation of rooftop solar PV systems in academic institutions, supporting renewable energy integration and sustainability initiatives. This research offers insights into the effects of tilt angles on energy generation and system performance, providing practical solutions for maximizing energy efficiency in educational buildings.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis and Performance Improvement of Lead-Free Perovskite Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Recently, researchers and scientists have shown a heightened interest in lead-free perovskite materials because of the toxicity issues associated with lead-based options. Tin (Sn), a group 14 metal similar to lead, has gained attention as a viable alternative. In our study, we employed the SCAPS-1D numerical analyzing tool for optimizing the performance of an n-i-p structured heterostructure solar cell which is perovskite-based (PSC), planar and lead-free, comprising CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (methylammonium tin iodide) as the intrinsic (i) and p-layer, with CZTSSe, MOO3, and NiO serving as the hole transport layers (BTL) and SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as the electron transport layer (ETL). The thickness of the ETL and the defect density of the HTL layer were carefully evaluated, noting that the absorption coefficient inversely correlates with defect density. Our observations revealed that as the HTL layer defect density increases, the device's performance diminishes. Through meticulous adjustment of the ETL's thickness, HTL's defect density, and temperature, we achieved a notable efficiency of 26.86%, with a short circuit current of 33.40 mA/cm2, an open circuit voltage of 0.99 V, and 81.43% fill factor for solar cell design (FTO/ SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/ CB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/ CZTSSe/ Au).

articleTitle: Implementation of Microstrip Patch Antenna Array for Detection of Brain Tumor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In this work, a microstrip patch antenna array designed specifically to detect brain tumors at 2.4 GHz, a frequency that is within the ISM frequency, is presented. The antenna array was meticulously designed to address the challenging issues related to brain tumour detection, while adhering to the safety rules outlined by IEEE standards. The antenna array is constructed using a FR-4 substrate, which has a relative permittivity of 4.3 F/m. The substrate has a thickness of 1.6 mm. The efficacy of the proposed microstrip patch antenna array in cancer detection is meticulously evaluated. The efficacy of the antenna array in detecting brain cancer is assessed by implanting a malignant tumour into a simulated model of the human brain. The simulation findings indicate that the reflectance coefficient experienced a shift of 7.34 dB due to the presence of a tumour. Additionally, the resonance frequency experiences a change of 3.2 MHz in the presence of a tumour. The detection exhibited a difference of 643.26% in gain, 7.77% in directivity, 7.77% in e-field, 2.57% in h-field, and 40.21% in SAR. The SAR is computed using a 10g tissue model. These values meet the safety standards set by the IEEE standard, confirming the feasibility of the suggested antenna for detecting brain cancer.

articleTitle: First Principle Investigation of Electronic, Optical, and Mechanical Properties of TlMCl3 (M= Ca, Cd) Under Pressure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Thallium (Tl)-based halide perovskites have developed as a hopeful candidate for various optoelectronic uses including solar cells, LEDs, photodetectors, etc. for their distinctive optical and electrical properties. TlMCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (M=Ca, Cd) are studied under the force of hydrostatics differing from 0 to 125 GPa and 0 to 200 GPa utilizing first-principles methods. The bandgap of TlCaCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> reduced from 3.953 eV to 1.924 eV under variation in pressures between 0 and 125 GPa causing an UV to visible area transition. The bandgap of TlCdCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> is reduced from 1.789 to 0 eV via changing pressure from 0 GPa to 200 GPa and the compound became metallic at 200 GPa. An increasing tendency of optical absorptivity, conductivity, and reflectivity is observed in both compounds under pressure. Both compounds are mechanically stable, and the ductility also increases with the applied pressure.

articleTitle: Novel Architecture of a Low Power D Flip-Flop Based Compact Frequency Divider for Wideband PLL Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In this study, a 90nm CMOS frequency divider utilizing D-type flip-flop integrated with a buffer circuit for enhanced performance at low voltage is introduced. The divider covers a wide frequency range from 2.496 GHz to 9.992 GHz, providing a tuning range of 120%. It operates efficiently within a low voltage range of 0 to 0.8 V, achieving optimized performance at 0.8 V. The power consumption varies from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.02325}\ \mu \mathbf{W}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{15.39}\ \mu \mathbf{W}$</tex>, with a notably low consumption of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{15.39}\ \mu \mathbf{W}$</tex> at 0.8 V. The proposed architecture exhibits favorable phase noise characteristics, achieving -138.3009 dBc/Hz at a 1 MHz offset frequency. To comprehensively evaluate the circuit's performance, the figure of merit (FOM) is calculated yielding values of -224.387 dBc/Hz or 7797.27 which demonstrates an exceptional balance between locking range and power dissipation. Also, the implemented divider occupies a compact area of only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.0000054584}\ \mathbf{mm}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex>. To assess the stability of the system across diverse environments, process corner and temperature sweep analysis is also conducted. To sum up, the proposed design effectively employs D-type flip-flops to achieve wide frequency range with minimal voltage, power consumption, and compact size suitable for various wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a 4-element Wideband MIMO Antenna for THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In this work, initially a rectangular microstrip patch antenna measuring (94.8 × 110 × 10) µm3 with a polyamide substrate has been analyzed and developed. The antenna has a bandwidth of 170 GHz (1.98 - 2.15 THz) and is tuned to resonate at a frequency of 2.08 THz. Its return loss is -26.733 dB, radiation efficiency is 92<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, and maximum gain is 6.35 dB. In addition, the MIMO technology has been implemented to improve performance. Its bandwidth is 210 GHz (1.98-2.19 THz), and it offers a reflection coefficient of -37.75 dB, a radiation efficiency of 95%, and a peak gain of 6.01 dB. The substrate of the four-element MIMO antenna measures (154.8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sup>170<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sup>10) µm3. The HFSS platform has been used to perform the modelling and simulation.

articleTitle: Enhancing Security in Multicasting Employing Generalized Receiver with MRC Diversity and Opportunistic Relaying Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper focuses on a secure wireless multi-casting under the employment of generalized receiver along with maximal ratio combining (MRC) diversity technique using opportunistic relaying technique. MRC diversity technique and opportunistic relaying technique mitigate the fading effect significantly and the generalized receiver is flexible to adaptive signal processing. The authors want to protect the transmitted signal from eavesdropping considering the effect of number of relays, receive side antenna number, eavesdropper side antenna number, multicast user number and eavesdropper number. In this issue the authors derived the closed form analytical expression for probability of non-zero secrecy multicast capacity (PNSMC) and secure outage probability for multicasting (SOPM) to ensure the secrecy in the presence of multiple eavesdroppers. These mathematical models are helpful to to realize the insight of the effects of aforementioned parameters. The numerical results show that, security in multicast network employing generalized receiver with MRC diversity technique is significantly affected by the number of relay, receive antenna, eavesdropper antenna, multicast user and eavesdropper, specially at low noise power region of eavesdropper.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transmission for Medical Devices: Harnessing Energy from RF Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) for medical equipment is a promising technology with the potential to revolutionize healthcare. It offers many advantages over traditional wire-based power delivery, such as increased convenience, reduced discomfort, and extended battery life. One promising approach to WPT for medical devices is to leverage the abundant RF signals in the environment. RF energy harvesting can power medical equipment without the need for batteries or wires, improving patient comfort and safety. This research makes several important contributions to the design of energy-harvesting circuits. Firstly, a nonlinear diode model is developed to accurately represent the diode's behavior within the circuit. This model helps in understanding how the diode performs in the circuit. Secondly, the input impedance of the rectifier circuit is calculated when connected to a load to ensure proper impedance matching. This ensures efficient power transfer from the energy source to the load. Lastly, an impedance-matching network is designed to maximize power transmission. The circuit's performance is evaluated through simulations, considering output voltage and efficiency factors.

articleTitle: Enhancing Wireless Power Transfer Efficiency for Medical Implants: A Performance Evaluation of Human Tissue Encapsulated Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Development in radio frequency (RF)-based wireless power transfer (WPT) is transforming implantable medical devices (IMDs)-including pacemakers, neurostimulators, and drug delivery systems-into cutting-edge technologies. The current research investigates these developments, focusing in particular on the creation and enhancement of implantable rectennas-which transform electromagnetic waves into DC power necessary for implantable medical devices-and their optimization. Our work addresses a variety of design factors, such as efficiency, bio-compatibility, and antenna size and frequency range. Additionally, it presents a human tissue model that incorporates safety precautions such as the specific absorption rate (SAR) to precisely represent antenna behavior within the body. Findings show that our rectennas outperform previous methods, achieving an amazing RF-to-DC conversion efficiency of up to 75.75%. The improvements made in 3D printing and materials greatly improve the efficiency and compactness of rectennas, which might revolutionize power management in biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Recurrent Neural Network Based Hybrid Deep Learning Architecture for Enhanced Network Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Growing cybercrime in an era of widespread internet access presents major challenges to network security, especially in the realm of intrusion detection. While deep learning and machine learning have revolutionized network intrusion detection by helping identify between attacks and regular network traffic, it is still difficult to detect a wide variety of attacks with high accuracy. Additionally, this task becomes more challenging due to the computational demands of analyzing largescale data. To address these challenges, we have proposed a novel approach utilizing a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) based recurrent neural network, integrated with Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture. The effectiveness of this model is assessed in our research in comparison to other deep learning techniques, such as basic RNN, LSTM, and GRU. Through extensive experimentation, our proposed hybrid CNN-LSTM model demonstrates superior performance, achieving 98.34% accuracy in multi-class classification and 98.7% accuracy in binary classification, with the most optimized publicly accessible CSE-CIC-IDS2018 dataset. Promising outcomes are also seen in important categorization metrics including F1-score, Precision, and Recall. Our results highlight the effectiveness of the integrated hybrid CNN-LSTM infrastructure as a strong classifier for cyberattack identification.

articleTitle: Integrated Power Generation Using Piezoelectric Sensors for Load Theft Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The use of low-power electronic devices has exploded in recent years. By attaching a piezoelectric sensor to the seaward location of an existing coastal structure, the features of a novel wave power producing system have been provided. When the sensor is attached to the structure, waves will strike the piezoelectric sensor and produce wave energy while also acting as a wave breaker. This method may be used to combine the functions of a wave-reducing structure with a renewable energy generator in a variety of coastal constructions. Multiple people depend on gadgets to make their life easier. Because of the rising demand for power from our handheld electronics, the world is becoming increasingly curious about the potential for harnessing renewable energy sources in our immediate environment. This work is learning how to create a piezoelectric generator. Using vibration and pressure, it is possible to generate energy, which can then be used for some other purpose (Like people walking). Project details how piezoelectric materials were used to generate and store energy from the vibrations caused by people's footsteps, and vehicle Pressure. Naturally occurring big vibration sources are another domain in which this idea shines. This work is also a precursor to the low-cost and simple piezoelectric energy harvesting model and also uses simulating tools like MATLAB.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Characterization of Natural Dye Sensitized Solar Cells With Red Spinach and Henna Extracts for Enhanced Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study evaluates the efficacy of different TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> paste formulations on natural dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) in indoor and outdoor settings. It investigates the impact of various factors, including electrolyte sheet thickness, industrial-grade TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and electrolyte concentration, on cell electrical characteristics and durability. Red spinach (Amaranthus cruentus) and henna (Lawsonia inermis) dyes are specifically highlighted as sensitizers. Accurate performance analysis is facilitated by controlled laboratory conditions. DSSCs created with these natural dyes exhibit diverse electrical behaviors under varying conditions. In comparative experiments conducted under the standard AM 1.5G solar spectrum suitable for Bangladesh's environment, red spinach-sensitized cells achieved an efficiency of 0.81%, significantly higher than the 0.018% efficiency of henna-sensitized cells.

articleTitle: Shallow Tuned DenseNet: A Lightweight Convolutional Neural Network Approach for Enhanced Skin Lesion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Skin lesions are irregularities on the skin, often harmless, though some may progress to skin cancer. Detecting them early is crucial for successful treatment and prevention of cancer development. Traditional detection methods involve significant expenses and testing. This study introduces an auto-mated system for classifying skin lesions using a Shallow Tuned DenseNet (STDN), a compact Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. We employ Transfer Learning (TL) by fine-tuning a pretrained DenseNet-169 model with additional lightweight layers, allowing the STDN to adapt to the PH<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> dataset's specific characteristics while remaining efficient. Initially, we utilize data augmentation techniques to address class imbalances within the dataset, improving model performance by reducing bias towards the majority class. The evaluation demonstrates a promising hundred percent accuracy with perfect F1-score and specificity. We attribute these results to effective transfer learning utilization, enhanced tuning, and partially to data augmentation, which mitigates overfitting and biases, facilitating robust feature extraction. Furthermore, we employ Grad-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping) to visualize and interpret the model's predictions, enhancing trust and comprehension. The proposed STDN model makes a significant contribution by achieving high accuracy with a lightweight design, offering a potentially cost-effective and efficient solution for automated skin lesion detection, thereby aiding in early cancer prevention.

articleTitle: Advancements in Holographic Image Enhancement: Leveraging Advanced Fresnel Algorithm for Improved Reconstructed Image Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This work focuses on enhancing the image quality of received holographic images in secure communication systems by utilizing an advanced Fresnel algorithm. Moreover, the work extends its investigation into refining the quality of reconstructed holographic images, delving deeper into methodologies to enhance their visual fidelity and overall perceptual clarity. The Fresnel algorithm, known for its fast processing and high-quality reconstruction, forms the backbone of our proposed method. Analyzing the algorithm's parameters and optimizing the hologram reconstruction and receiving process aims to mitigate artifacts and distortions, thereby achieving highly improved image quality of the received holographic image. Our approach leverages advanced computational techniques to enhance the resolution, contrast, and overall visual clarity of reconstructed holographic images. Through rigorous experimentation and comparative analysis, we demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed method in significantly improving the image quality of received holographic data. This research contributes to the ongoing development of secure communication systems, offering practical insights and methodologies for advancing the capabilities of computer-generated holography in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Towards Early Dengue Diagnosis in Bangladesh: A Non-Invasive Prediction Model Based on Symptoms and Local Trends
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Dengue fever is a significant public health concern in Bangladesh, with a rising number of cases highlighting the need for early and accurate diagnosis. This study proposes a novel approach for early dengue diagnosis using a non-invasive predictive model based on external symptoms and local trends. Two datasets are prepared in the context of Bangladesh, one containing dengue cases with only external symptoms along with the month and district of affection. The other dataset contains statistical data on active dengue cases per month in Bangladesh from 2016 to 2023 and is used to capture seasonal trends. The number of cases is taken district-wise to determine the relation between dengue affection and active dengue cases in nearby areas. A two-step machine learning-based model is proposed, using machine learning-based time series forecasting models including the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Prophet models. The Prophet model performs better than the LSTM model, with lower MAE and RMSE values. A new dataset is created by merging the prediction of the first model with the external symptoms dataset's month and location attributes. Random Forest and XGBoost classifiers are used for case prediction on the second dataset and the merged dataset. The merged dataset has a top 82.3% accuracy, while the external symptoms dataset has a 92.5% accuracy. This approach aims to provide an efficient solution to improve early dengue diagnosis, ultimately facilitating timely intervention and resource allocation for effective disease management.

articleTitle: Towards Sustainable Aquaculture: An IoT-Driven Indoor Fish Farming System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study presents an innovative IoT-driven fish farming system to enhance aquaculture efficiency and sustainability. The system utilizes Arduino microcontrollers integrated with DS18B20 temperature sensors and analog pH meters to enable real-time monitoring and control of environmental conditions. Key functionalities include automated fish feeding, dynamic feed quantity calculations, and pH adjustments using a mobile application interface. The system demonstrated effective temperature and pH regulation, though minor variations were noted in the automated feeding mechanism. Alerts for critical conditions were generally timely but occasionally delayed during simultaneous updates. This IoT-based solution significantly improves fish farming management, contributing to the optimal well-being of aquatic species.

articleTitle: Uncovering Patterns of Depression in Engineering and Medical Students Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the evaluation of mental health challenges faced by engineering and medical students in Bangladesh, utilizing advanced machine learning and statistical methods. Data were collected through comprehensive questionnaires, focusing on socio-demographic, academic, and mental health variables. The dataset, including responses from 834 students, was preprocessed and split into two subsets: one for medical students and another for engineering students. The study utilized Student's T-Test and Fisher's Exact Test to identify 16 key features associated with mental health challenges. Following feature selection, a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier was used to evaluate the impact of these features on depression prediction. The evaluation metrics included accuracy, ROC AUC, precision, recall, and F1 score, allowing for a comprehensive assessment of the models' performance. By leveraging advanced machine learning techniques, this research seeks to uncover patterns and predictors of depression that traditional studies often overlook. The findings aim to provide targeted insights into the factors contributing to mental health challenges in these student populations, guiding effective interventions. The paper emphasizes the global relevance of the study, as mental health challenges among university students are prevalent worldwide.

articleTitle: THD Reduction in Switched Diode Multilevel Inverter Using Improved Grey Wolf Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of Switched Diode Multilevel Inverters (SMLIs) for Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) reduction using various optimization algorithms: Flower Pollination Algorithm (FPA), Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), and Improved Grey Wolf Optimizer (IGWO). Results show that IGWO outperforms both FPA and GWO, achieving the lowest THD levels across different modulation indices. The minimum THD found by IGWO is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.90 \%$</tex>. FPA exhibits higher THD values, especially at higher modulation indices, while GWO shows intermediate performance. THD analysis reveals the sensitivity of harmonic distortion to modulation index changes. The study highlights the significance of optimization algorithms in multilevel inverter design for efficient power conversion. IGWO proves effective in reducing harmonic distortion, ensuring compliance with quality standards, and enhancing overall SMLI performance. This research contributes to advancing multilevel inverter technology and provides valuable insights into optimizing SMLIs for improved efficiency.

articleTitle: Modified Approach for Solving Hemodynamic Model by fMRI Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The hemodynamic model is a crucial method for effectively monitoring and potentially predicting brain activity. Researching the solution of the hemodynamic model is a feasible task. Three popular techniques in the field of biomedical engineering are utilised to solve the hemodynamic model parameters, hidden states, and estimate blood oxygen level dependent (BOLD) signal from fMRI pictures. The dynamic expectation maximisation (DEM) is a commonly used technique for inverting a hemodynamic model. Both the square root cubature Kalman smoothing (SCKS) and the recently introduced confounds SCKS (CSCKS) are derived from the cubature Kalman filtering (CKF) approach. The standard algorithms provide the necessary measurement, but their accuracy is lower compared to the suggested new CSCKS technique, which has improved algorithms. The new CSCKS algorithm provides hidden state estimates that are 89% accurate, while the old CSCKS, SCKS, and DEM methods provide estimates that are 82%, 53%, and 36% accurate, respectively. Under identical parameter conditions, the new CSCKS algorithm demonstrates an accuracy that is 5%, 1.5%, and 16.07% higher than the old CSCKS method in estimating biophysical parameters, signal to interference ratio (SIR) of the BOLD response, and vascular signal of blood flow, respectively.

articleTitle: Development of Three Phase High Power Smart Meter for Energy Management Monitoring System in UniKL MSI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Energy efficiency is defined as using energy in the most efficient way to provide the same service that could have been provided less efficiently. Low energy efficiency will increase greenhouse gas emissions, demand for energy import, and high costs for electrical bills and economy-wide levels. This paper discusses the development of a 3-phase high-power smart energy meter using the Internet of Things (IoT). This meter was designed using a NodeMCU ESP8266 as the main controller device. Three PZEM-004T modules and Split Coil Current Transformer (CT) were the main sensors used in this project. The NodeMCU with the built-in Wi-Fi module allows this system to communicate wirelessly with the cloud server and mobile application. The accuracy of power data measurements proposed by the Smart Energy Monitoring System (SEMS) was tested by experimenting in a laboratory. The result shows all the data measurements of power usage proposed by SEMS had less than 10% error compared with the Power Analyzer. This demonstrated that SEMS had high accuracy and was equivalent to existing measurement devices on the market.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of IoT-Based Manhole Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper introduces an Internet of Things (IoT) based manhole monitoring system to improve traditional methods. The system employs various sensors, including temperature, humidity, ultrasonic, and gas sensors, integrated with a microcontroller (NodeMCU) to collect real-time data on water levels, temperature, humidity, methane, and ammonia. This data is transmitted to a cloud server, allowing for monitoring via a mobile app and web dashboard. Besides the constructed network of devices enhances the accuracy of blockage detection. The system ensures ethical engineering, legal compliance, and financial sustainability, aligning with Sustainable Development Goals. Real-time monitoring facilitates prompt responses to potential threats, enhancing maintenance efficiency and safety. Experimental results validate the system's effectiveness. At the same time, cost analysis reveals significant long-term savings compared to manual monitoring, making it a viable and advanced solution for urban infrastructure management.

articleTitle: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) Classification from Microscopic Images Using CNN Model ‘ALLNet’
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Leukemia is a common blood cancer that affects people of all ages and is one of the major causes of death, presenting a serious threat to world health. In this study, we have proposed a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model called’ ALLNet ‘ for the precise diagnosis and classification of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) in human bone marrow images. The model distinguishes between immature lymphoblasts and normal cells. Additionally, we performed a comparative analysis with a few unique CNN models and six pre-trained models, utilizing both Transfer Learning and Fine-Tuning techniques. The ‘ALLNet’ model achieved a high validation accuracy of 93.05%, a test accuracy of 93.43%, and a corresponding F1-score of 93.43%, with Roc curve area of 0.97. In terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, our proposed model performed better than all the models included in this study as well as other models that already exist. The ‘ALLNet’ demonstrates effectiveness and promise as a reliable method for classifying leukemia. The ‘ALLNet’ is a robust tool for medical professionals to accurately diagnose and classify acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) using bone marrow images. It offers the potential to improve patient care by aiding in early and accurate diagnosis, leading to timely treatment interventions. Additionally, it showcases the capability of CNN models in medical image analysis and classification tasks, contributing to advancements in healthcare technology.

articleTitle: High-Sensitivity Sensor for Sucrose Detection with Asymmetric Elliptical Core and Gold Coating
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This work presents for a new exposed core surface plasmon resonance (SPR) biosensor that makes use of a photonic crystal fiber with an asymmetrical elliptic air hole (PCF), which is renowned for its exceptional sensibility. The gold-plated fiber of this versatile sensor enables it to detect changes in refractive index (RI) for analytes over a wide range of 1.28 to 1.42. Specifically focusing on RI changes at the external surface, the sensor demonstrates impressive sensing performance, including an prime wavelength sensitivity regarding 97,000 nm/RIU as well as a prime amplitude sensitivity regarding 529.20 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. Additionally, it achieves the resolution regarding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{9.09}\times \mathbf{10}^{-\mathbf{6}}$</tex> RIU, the FOM is 170 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, the FWHM is also 570 nm, and here a detection of accuracy is 0.016666nm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. Utilizing a concentration range of 0% to 45% over time, the suggested sensor is useful for monitoring sucrose solutions. Beyond sucrose, the sensor demonstrates promising sensing capabilities for identifying various biochemical and organic samples, making it a valuable tool in biomedical sensing, lower RI analysis, and chemical analysis. Its structure, featuring eight elliptical air holes, is straightforward and easily manufacturable using existing technologies, thus facilitating practical application.

articleTitle: NeuroMindscape: Deep Learning Unraveling Alzheimer's Stages Through MRI-Based Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: A degenerative condition, Alzheimer's disease can result in a gradual deterioration of the capacity to carry out basic tasks, often beginning with mild memory loss. Alzheimer's disease is the predominant contributor to the onset of dementia, affecting approximately 1 in 9 adults aged 65 and older (10.7%) [14]. Lately, there has been a lot of promise in employing deep learning, especially the Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), in various medical imaging research works, including Alzheimer's Disease (AD). This research focuses on improving Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for accurate classification of 4 stages of dementia - mild, moderate, non-mild and very mild. This research introduces a model comprising seven layers, showcasing less complexity compared to its predecessors. Despite its simplicity, it demonstrates remarkable proficiency in multi-class classification tasks, achieving high-performance levels. With this model, the publicly available Kaggle Alzheimer's Disease (AD) dataset [16] was accessed, which contains 6400 MRI images with the total size of 36 Megabytes, and another Kaggle dataset [17] which adopted GAN (Generative adversarial network) based approach on the former dataset to produce synthetic images to address the imbalance issue. Using the original Kaggle Alzheimer's dataset and through methods of traditional augmentation to balance out of the classes, The proposed model successfully distinguished between the four stages of the disease with 97.05% accuracy which outperformed most of its other predeceasing CNN models, and on the Kaggle GAN-based dataset [17] the model achieved 97% accuracy.

articleTitle: Precision Death Forecasting of Dengue Outbreaks in Bangladesh by Blending Statistical and Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Dengue fever, spread by Aedes mosquitoes, presents a formidable global public health challenge. Despite progress in predictive modeling, the rising incidence and complexity of dengue necessitate more precise forecasting techniques. This study leverages a comprehensive dataset from Bangladesh, spanning 2019 to 2023, to improve dengue outbreak predictions by using hybrid models that blend traditional statistical methods with advanced machine learning algorithms. The research employs a Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) model, along with XGBoost and Random Forest Regression, to predict dengue incidence based on temporal and climatic variables. The dataset consists of 900 daily records, capturing crucial details such as date, month, year, and dengue cases to reflect seasonal trends impacting disease transmission. The results indicate that the XGBoost model, enhanced with features like DayOfWeek and Month, markedly surpasses other models. It achieved the lowest Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 2.6108 and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 1.6158, demonstrating superior predictive accuracy. Conversely, the SARIMA model, despite its ability to capture temporal patterns, showed limitations in managing non-linear trends, resulting in a higher RMSE.These findings emphasize the effectiveness of combining machine learning techniques with time series analysis to forecast dengue trends, offering a vital tool for public health officials to apply timely interventions. This study underscores the significance of integrating models and feature engineering to enhance the precision of health predictions, thus contributing to more effective dengue management strategies.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis on the Elevated Expressway in Bangladesh: A Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: User comments on social media or any video streaming platforms show how people feel about something, including different opinions, feelings, and problems of people interacting with it. It can assist people and organizations in making wellinformed choices by offering insightful information on how people feel about a topic or issue. The Elevated Expressway is a crucial infrastructure in Bangladesh and a controversial project that has sparked public debate and criticism. The 46.73 km road project connecting Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport to Kutubkhali on the Dhaka-Chittagong Highway has eased the commute time from the Airport to Farmgate from over an hour to 10 minutes. Regarding this project, People's comments on YouTube as a digital platform for voicing their opinions and contributing to a shared narrative that goes beyond traditional media. In this work, we examine users' sentiments about Elevated Expressway from YouTube comments, employing various Machine Learning (ML) algorithms and Deep Learning (ML) architecture. Based on these analyses, the BERT architecture arises as the most satisfying model, with an accuracy of 84.34% and a macro f1 score of 80.14% for classifying public sentiment as positive, negative, or neutral.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Framework Based on Attention Integrated Customized DenseNet201 Architecture for Multi-Class Skin Lesion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Skin lesions encompass abnormal skin changes, with some evolving into skin cancer if untreated; hence, early detection is vital. Automatic detection utilizing Deep Learning (DL) techniques can enhance accessibility and affordability of diagnosis, overcoming barriers posed by extensive testing and associated costs. However, in most deep learning (DL) research, the issue of imbalanced class distribution is often overlooked, as researchers frequently rely on transfer learning (TL) with pre-trained models without adequate customization or fine-tuning. Consequently, these models suffer in extracting fine-grained details, and there is an absence of analysis regarding the model's decision-making process. Therefore, this paper presents a TL-based explainable Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Framework (MFFF) to address the above-mentioned challenges. This framework utilizes pre-trained DenseNet201 with three attention mechanisms: Channel Attention (CA), Soft Attention (SA), and Squeeze and Excitation Attention (SEA). The top layers of DenseNet201 are customized and fine-tuned with three separate series of convolutional blocks, each comprising diverse attention blocks to extract relevant features at different scales. Finally, the extracted features from these convolutional blocks are concatenated to produce more fine-grained features. An empirical evaluation on a publicly available dataset demonstrates that our proposed MFFF achieves 97.15% accuracy, outperforming other state-of-the-art research. Furthermore, Gradient Class Activation Map (Grad-CAM) is employed to highlight crucial regions and explore the decision-making process of the black box Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Framework (MFFF), assisting dermatologists in effective decision-making.

articleTitle: An Empirical Analysis of 5.4Tbps MDM-WDM Hybrid Network for 100km Multimode Communication Using Multimode Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Medium distance transmission is absolute for the application of high-power signal transmission where multimode fiber (MMF) is a more cost-effective choice over single-mode optical fiber. This study presents an optimized approach that successfully demonstrates a state-of-the-art technology known as multi-level multiplexing, which combines wavelength division multiplexing and mode division multiplexing for a mediumdistance communication scheme over multimode fiber spanning 100km. The system achieved a transmission capacity of 5.4Tbps using 40 WDM channels while preserving signal quality and optimal power levels in the output. The goal is to demonstrate a new strategy that can considerably improve transmission capacity while maintaining signal quality. Bit error rate, Q factor, and eye diagram are discussed for concluding and comparing the transmission quality.

articleTitle: Improper Implementation of Transport Layer Security: Impact on Android Applications and Man-in-the-Middle Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In this paper, we have analyzed the impact of improper implementation of Transport Layer Security (TLS) in Android applications. Communication security in Android applications is largely dependent on Transport Layer Security. For instance, data encryption, data integrity, authentication, trust-building, network attack prevention, and API and web service security are all provided by it. TLS preserves confidence and aids in preventing the unwanted exposure of sensitive data. However, improper implementation of TLS can pose a serious threat to the cybersecurity of an application. Therefore, software developers should ensure the security of applications, foster client confidence, and adhere to legal standards by skillfully implementing TLS. In this paper, we have chosen 25 miscellaneous Android applications and performed static analysis on them. Furthermore, we have identified various improper implementations of TLS in these applications. The riskiest TLS implementations in these applications include insufficient verification of the TLS certificate chain, invalid TLS certificates, insufficient checking of the TLS certificate validity, and insecure WebViews usage. For these vulnerable implementations of TLS, some applications are prone to a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack. At last, we have provided the best practices of TLS implementations for Android applications. In addition, we have provided remediation for the vulnerabilities so that applications can be protected against MitM attacks.

articleTitle: Ransomware Detection Utilizing Ensemble Based Interpretable Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Ransomware, a form of malicious software, encrypts victim data and renders it inaccessible until a ransom is paid. Different ransomware variants employ various tactics to avoid detection during their attacks. Understanding the techniques used in ransomware development and deployment is crucial to counter these threats. This study presents a stacked ensemble-based machine learning (ML) approach for ransomware detection. The ensemble model consists of Naive Bayes (NB), Random Forest (RF), and K-Nearest Neibors (KNN) as base classifiers and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) as meta-classifiers. Additionally, Explainable AI (XAI) utilizing LIME and SHAP has been applied to gain insights into prediction outcomes and validate model correctness. The use of LIME and SHAP ensures the inter-pretability of the model, which is a crucial factor in real-world implications. The research employs a publicly available dataset and evaluates the model using multiple metrics. Experimental results reveal that the proposed model achieves an impressive accuracy of 98.57%. The model is benchmarked against existing ML techniques, demonstrating its superior performance.

articleTitle: Classification Model for Autism Spectrum Disorder Individuals: Utilizing Facial Grid-Wise Emotion Features and Dual-Branch Visual Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) poses challenges in social interaction and attention, often identifiable through facial emotions due to the absence of definitive medical tests. This study introduces the Dual-branch CNN-based visual transformation model (Db-CNN-VTM) for ASD identification. Pre-processing and geometric data augmentation enhance model robustness, while feature extraction via transformation-coded convolutional neural network (Tr-CNN) and feature fusion using a residual network refined classification. Optimization through the hunger game search optimization (HGSO) method determines hyperparameters. Comparative analysis with ResNet, AlexNet, CNN, and DNN models demonstrates Db-CNN-VTM's superior performance with accuracy 96.91%, precision 96.91%, recall 96.89%, F1-score 96.90%, specificity 96.89%, FPR 0.03%, kappa 93.80%, MCC 93.80%, and MSE 0.03%.

articleTitle: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Multi-Class Skin Lesion Classification While Resolving Class Imbalance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Skin lesions are indicative of various skin diseases, including serious conditions like melanoma, which can be life-threatening if not detected early. Automated systems for analyzing dermatoscopic images have shown promise in improving diagnostic accuracy. However, many existing studies rely on pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures without customization, leading to potential biases and suboptimal performance. In this study, we propose a customized DenseNet121 architecture tailored for skin lesion classification. We address class imbalance issues through data augmentation and fine-tune the model to extract fine-grained features. Our method surpasses other cutting-edge models in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, sensitivity, and root mean square (ROC) values. Furthermore, we utilise Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) to visually represent the decision-making process of the model. The next study will prioritise the validation of the model using a wide range of datasets and the integration of lesion-related information to enhance its performance.

articleTitle: Improved Skin Lesion Detection with Double Layer Concatenated DenseNet Using Transfer Learning and Attention Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Skin that becomes unnaturally elevated, discoloured, or behaves in another unusual way may indicate a more serious health issue, such as skin cancer. Lesions on the skin, on the other hand, deviate from the skin's typical appearance and may point to more serious health issues. Accurate localization of diseased areas is challenging due to the complexity and expense of diagnostic tests; however, early lesion detection is essential for cancer prevention and diagnosis. The innovative automated method described in this article relies on Transfer Learning (TL), and its fundamental component is the use of DenseNet models. We have fine-tuned these models to repeatedly concatenate three attention modules, effectively extracting salient data for lesion identification. Before using concatenation to generate final features, it is necessary to fine-tune and incorporate attention mechanisms into all DenseNet models. For each version of DenseNet, the outcome of carrying out this method is Double Layer Concatenated DenseNet (DLCD). Using the ISIC 2019 dataset as an example, the proposed model reaches a remarkable 91.61% accuracy. Using GradCAM to pinpoint the precise region for categorization is one way to enhance the explainability of the architecture. We improve the study's accuracy while advancing the use of TL and other augmentation approaches. The results of this research provide techniques to improve the identification and early detection of skin lesions, perhaps resulting in a reduction in the incidence of skin cancer.

articleTitle: IoT Enabled Soil Fertilizer Monitoring and Recommendation System in the Context of Bangladeshi Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Soil fertility plays a pivotal role in enhancing agricultural productivity, which serves as the cornerstone of human sustenance and livelihood. Critical soil chemical elements such as nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), pH, temperature, and moisture significantly influence soil fertility. Achieving a bountiful harvest hinges on accurately assessing soil composition and applying fertilizers judiciously at the right time. However, due to a dearth of expertise and improper fertilizer application practices, many farmers struggle to cultivate high-quality crops. Traditional soil nutrient assessment methods involving laborious soil sampling and laboratory analysis are both time-consuming and costly. This study proposes an efficient Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled soil fertilizer monitoring and recommendation system aimed at providing farmers with data-driven insights into soil parameters and weather conditions, including soil type and characteristics. Utilizing an array of sensors, the system continuously gathers soil fertility data from farm fields, transmitting via Wireless sensor network (WSN) to a cloud-based database. The best fertilizer will be determined based on various parameters for the specific crop. The IoT-enabled system monitors soil parameters (N, P, K, temperature, pH, moisture, soil type, and rainfall) in real-time, facilitating informed decision-making for farmers. Leveraging this data, a predictive model is employed to recommend suitable fertilizer types, tailored to individual soil conditions. By curbing unnecessary fertilizer expenses and reducing reliance on manual labor in crop management, the proposed solution aims to bolster agricultural productivity. Consequently, it is poised to contribute significantly to national agricultural output and economic growth.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Structural, Electronic, Mechanical and Optical Properties Through Density Function Theory of Bilayer Germanium Carbide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Bilayer two-dimensional (2D) crystal have received substantial interest because of their remarkable features, including enhanced optical absorption, superconductivity, and adjustable bandgap. These properties surpass those of the currently available monolayer 2D materials. We primarily deal with two-dimensional bilayer germanium carbide's (2D-GeC) optical, vibrational, and electronic structure using an exact first-principles density functional theory (DFT) investigation. The electrical bandgap of bilayer 2D-GeC increases from 1.21 eV at the material's direct K-point to about 1.23 eV when the spin-orbit coupling (SOC) effect is included. The exceptional ability of bilayer 2D-GeC to absorb light in both the visible and infrared (IR) bands causes changes in its optical properties, including its real and imaginary dielectric spectra as well as its electron energy loss function (EELF).

articleTitle: DeepFlowNet: Deep Learning Based Daily Water Flow Forecasting of Test River
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: River flow Forecasting is crucial for managing hazards and water resources, particularly in hilly areas where there is a significant reliance on downstream flows. In water resource management, incorporating methods such as time series, conceptual modeling, and artificial neural networks (ANNs) improves river flow forecasting accuracy. In this research, three most popular deep learning frameworks such as Deep Neural Network (DNN), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and Long Short Term Memory Network (LSTM) have been employed to forecast the flow of river Test accurately. This dataset contains the daily gauged flow rate(m^3/sec) of the River Test, and climatic data (precipitation and temperature). A set of ten input combinations with lagged river flow values are developed. The target value is smoothed using a Gaussian filter with a sigma value of 5. The results show that LSTM performed the best followed by GRU and DNN. In measurable terms, LSTM, GRU and DNN models was demonstrated by R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>= 0.93, 0.915, and 0.876, RMSE = 0.393, 0.412, and 0.498, MAE = 0.247, 0.257, and 0.323, MAPE 0.337, 0.328, and 0.432, and MSE = 0.155, 0.169, and 0.248 respectively. The results strengthen the argument that deep learning algorithms particularly LSTM outperforms other above-mentioned algorithms for forecasting rivers flow with supreme accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimizing Depth and Ego-Motion Estimation with Swin Transformer: A Comprehensive Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Accurately perceiving depth and motion within single images is crucial in computer vision, especially for applications like autonomous vehicles and virtual environments. While convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown effectiveness, their limitation in capturing wider contexts restricts current network topologies to local processing, hindering the potential of self-supervised methods. This study introduces a novel method utilizing the Swin Transformer to extract precise information from images of varying sizes, employing advanced techniques such as window and shifted-window-based attention mechanisms. Coupled with an efficient decoder network, this enhances depth estimation. Extensively tested on datasets like KITTI, this method consistently outperforms traditional approaches in predicting depth and motion accurately. Challenges remain, notably in discerning obscured items and navigating complex environments, compounded by limited dataset evaluations. Nevertheless, this approach shows promise for practical deployment, given its adaptability to diverse scenarios, underscoring the significant potential of leveraging the Swin Transformer for improved depth and motion estimation in computer vision systems.

articleTitle: A Cost-Effective Real-Time Water Quality Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Ensuring access to safe drinking water is critically important, particularly in regions facing scarcity and contamination challenges. This paper presents a cost-effective, IoT-based water quality monitoring system specifically designed for rural areas. The system measures key water parameters, including pH, turbidity, temperature, electrical conductivity, and TDS. It integrates an ESP8266 for data acquisition, filtering, and transmission to RTWQMS, a real-time web-based application for data visualization, which utilizes an inference engine for binary decision-making. The system's architecture is structured into three layers: the Physical Layer (sensors), the Network Layer (ESP8266), and the Application Layer (RTWQMS). This project aims to provide an affordable solution for continuous water quality assessment, thereby ensuring safe drinking water in underserved communities. Future developments will include the integration of an expert system for decision-making using advanced machine learning algorithms for multi-class classification of water quality.

articleTitle: Advancing Cardiac Diagnosis via Machine Learning Techniques to Identify Anomalous ECG Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Early detection of cardiac abnormalities through ECG signal analysis is crucial for improving patient outcomes. This study evaluates machine learning techniques—K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree (DT), and Random Forest (RF)—to classify ECG patterns into arrhythmia (ARR), congestive heart failure (CHF), and normal sinus rhythm (NSR) efficiently. Key ECG features include the Stress Index (SI), Vagal Sympathetic Effect (VSE), and Respiratory Sinus Arrhythmia (RSA). SI shows high mean values for NSR (3.86), intermediate for ARR (2.68), and low for CHF (1.32), indicating stress variations among these conditions.
