VSE values are lowest in CHF (0.52), highest in ARR (0.78), and intermediate in NSR (0.68), reflecting differences in autonomic regulation. RSA values demonstrate a similar pattern: NSR at 3.91 ms, CHF at 2.22 ms, and ARR at 5.21 ms, showing varying levels of respiratory influence on heart rate. These numerical distinctions underscore the different physiological impacts of each cardiac condition. Among the classification techniques, Random Forest consistently outperforms others, making it particularly effective for early diagnosis. This comparative analysis highlights the importance of specific ECG features and the performance of RF in accurately distinguishing between ARR, CHF, and NSR, enhancing timely and precise cardiac condition diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Power Allocation in 5G Homogeneous Network Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing power allocation within 5G homogeneous networks using deep reinforcement learning (DRL). The proposed method involves a two-stage training paradigm, beginning with offline deep Q learning (DQL) to train a dueling double deep Q network (D3QN) in a simulated environment. Subsequent online fine-tuning with real-world data further enhances the D3QN's performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the D3QN outperforms existing DQL-trained networks, achieving superior averaged sum rates and showcasing heightened adaptability across various user densities. This approach offers a promising solution for efficiently managing power allocation in wireless cellular networks, particularly within the context of 5G homogeneous network scenarios.

articleTitle: Advancements in Jute Leaf Disease Detection: A Comprehensive Study Utilizing Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Detecting diseases in jute leaves is difficult due to the variability in how the diseases appear. Manually identifying these diseases is challenging because it requires expert knowledge and visual inspections take a lot of time. Machine Learning (ML) offers a promising solution to these challenges by automating the detection process. However, research in this area is limited due to the lack of specific datasets. This study aims to address this by creating a comprehensive dataset of 10,800 high-quality images of jute leaf diseases. The main goal is to develop a robust system for classifying jute leaves into three categories: Yellow Mosaic, Powdery Mildew, and Healthy. Our methodology involved extensive image preprocessing, including resizing and various augmentation techniques, to enhance the dataset's diversity and ensure model robustness. We trained various ML and Deep Learning (DL) models and conducted a comparative analysis of their performance. Additionally, we compared our approach with the state-of-the-art methods. The results showed that DL models, particularly Inception V3, achieved an outstanding accuracy of 99.98\%, compared to 89.75\% for Random Forest (RF). This highlights the potential of DL techniques in improving the accuracy of jute leaf disease detection. Our findings contribute to better disease management strategies and increased productivity in jute cultivation.

articleTitle: Enhancing Chili Plant Disease Detection: A Comprehensive Ensemble Approach Utilizing Pre-Trained Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Chili is one of the most prominent crops of Bangladesh. Chilis are great at boosting the human immune system and contributing to overall good health. But every year, chili production is hampered due to various diseases. Deep learning-based models can mitigate this issue by detecting plant diseases quickly and accurately. This research aims to make an ensemble technique approach harnessing various pre-trained CNN models to classify healthy chili leaves and chili diseases such as yellowish, leaf spot (fungi), and whitefly infestations. We used CNN models such as MobileNetV2, ResNet152, EfficientNetB7, EfficientNetV2B0, InceptionV3, ResNet50, DenseNet121, and DenseNet201. The Chili dataset was approved by BARI (Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute). We examined the outcomes of each model with three optimizers, Adam, RMSRrop, and SGD, where RMSProp gave the best outcome overall. Then, ensemble techniques were implemented by combining two variations for each of the top three best-performed CNN models, subsequently comparing their performance. The proposed ensemble model is EfficientNetV2B0, with EfficientNetB7 outperforming all the existing deep learning models and achieving a maximum accuracy of 99.56%.

articleTitle: IoT-Driven Smart Workplace Ecosystem with RFID Security and Environmental Monitoring Featuring App Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In the era of technological advancements, the integration of smart automation into workplaces has become pivotal for enhancing efficiency, security, and employee well-being. This research introduces a comprehensive smart workplace system leveraging RFID security, attendance tracking, environmental monitoring, and a custom mobile application. The system aims to redefine conventional workplace dynamics by seamlessly integrating these technologies. Primary objectives include fortifying access control through RFID technology, optimizing attendance record-keeping using cloud-based solutions, and fostering a secure, energy-efficient environment through automated features and sensor networks. The custom mobile application, crafted with MIT App Inventor, serves as a central hub, providing authorized personnel with real-time access to crucial workplace data. It offers insights into appliance usage statistics and employee attendance, enabling informed decisions and control over appliances for optimal energy usage. Results showcase the successful implementation of RFID security protocols, accurate attendance tracking, and real-time environmental monitoring. The discussion interprets these results, addresses implementation challenges, and proposes avenues for future refinement.

articleTitle: Towards Underwater Sustainability with AIoT: Underwater Trash Management System Comprised of YOLOv8 with IoT-Applied Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Effective techniques for managing rubbish underwater are essential due to growing environmental concerns about contamination under the sea. In this research, we offer a novel method for efficient underwater trash detection and management that makes use of the Internet of Things (IoT) and the YOLOV8 object detection model. Using YOLOV8, the suggested system seeks to identify and categorize underwater garbage in real-time. It then uses IoT devices for segmentation and management. We outline the suggested system's design, talk about how YOLOV8 integrates with Internet of Things gadgets, and provide experimental results to validate the system's efficacy. Our findings suggest that the suggested strategy has great potential to advance efforts to manage undersea waste and manage pollution as well as segment using 6-DOF Robotic Arm. The IoT based system allows remote monitoring of trash density and location along with the raspberry-pi server-based video feed allows the users to suitably monitor aquatic conditions remotely. The fusion of IoT and deep learning on YOLO v8 model opens gateway for water sustainability and enhances further opportunities in employing robotic arm-based trash collection system.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach to Analyze the Relationship Between Gender, Height, Weight, and Basal Metabolic Rate from Face Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In response to existing limitations, a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) model tailored for facial attribute estimation is introduced in this study. The methodology encompasses meticulous data preprocessing techniques, including dataset splitting, resizing, cleaning, augmentation, and cropping, to ensure the integrity of the dataset. Through rigorous real-world testing, remarkable accuracy in predicting gender, height, weight, and basal metabolic rate (BMR) from facial photos is demonstrated by our CNN architecture. Notably, unlike conventional approaches where BMR is directly estimated from facial images, three output neurons are employed by our model to simultaneously predict gender, height, and weight, which are sub-sequently utilized for BMR calculation. A primary contribution is made through the development of a comprehensive methodology that advances the reliability of facial attribute estimation by achieving an outstanding accuracy of 98.50% on our dataset named Face-ete and a commendable accuracy of 88.29% on another dataset. Our model outperforms the second-best model by percentage relative improvement factors of 2.19 and 4.28 in terms of BMR prediction accuracy for the “Faceere” and the other dataset, respectively. This work represents a significant step forward in the field of facial attribute estimation.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Hydrogen Fuel Cell Vehicles in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Climate change is a pressing issue of the twenty-first century, exacerbated by the continuous burning of fossil fuels. In Bangladesh, the transportation sector contributes 20% of annual net carbon emissions, predominantly powered by fossil-based fuels. Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicles (HFCVs) present an up-and-coming solution, characterized by zero tailpipe emissions and exceptional efficiency, particularly suited for long-distance travel. This research employs a detailed SIMULINK model to analyze HFCV behavior and efficiency under Bangladesh driving conditions. It also assesses the net CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions of HFCVs throughout their lifecycle, from hydrogen production to vehicle operation. Scenario analysis compares environmental impacts with conventional internal combustion engines, revealing HFCVs' 20% higher efficiency and peak power utilization of about 45% at each charging-discharging cycle. This study contributes valuable insights into sustainable transportation solutions in Bangladesh, aiding the optimization of HFCVs for regional needs. Utilizing Simulink ensures accuracy in capturing the dynamic interlinkage within HFCV systems, advancing clean energy technologies in the Bangladeshi automotive sector.

articleTitle: Student Distraction Detection and Concentration Analysis via Transfer Learned Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In the midst of the significant shift from offline to online education, accurately measuring student concentration and identifying distractions have become crucial. Many institutions face difficulties in monitoring their students remotely. With limited existing research addressing this issue comprehensively, this work offers a groundbreaking study on the application of deep learning techniques to tackle these challenges. Leveraging a newly curated dataset specifically designed for the online learning environment, this study employs advanced convolutional neural networks (CNNs) such as DenseNet201, InceptionV3, Xception, and EfficientNetB6 through transfer learning methodologies. Extensive experimentation and analysis were conducted across 15 different classes, resulting in an impressive accuracy of 98.27%. This work not only makes a vital contribution to educational technology but also provides valuable insights into enhancing student engagement and concentration in the digital age. By demonstrating the efficacy of these advanced CNN models, this study paves the way for more effective monitoring and support systems in online education, ensuring that students remain focused and engaged in their virtual learning environments.

articleTitle: Review on Wearable Antennas and Circuits: Materials, Designs, Applications and Future Direction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Biomedicine and radio frequency (RF) engineering have changed the way we monitor our health through soft, wearable technology. These devices must be extremely flexible, safe for the body, and function well. So, we're updating existing electronic components, such as sensors and antennas, to meet these requirements. A lot of research has been done on this recently. This review will look at novel materials for flexible, efficient wearable technology, as well as improved designs to make them even more effective. We'll also discuss how these devices are employed in medical sensing and what may come next in this field.

articleTitle: A CNN-Based Approach for Room Number Detection Using Drone in Indoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The revolutionary development of drone technology has significantly transformed various sectors such as security, construction, and transportation. By using computer vision and artificial intelligence, drones can now autonomously execute tasks that previously relied on human intervention, resembling intelligent robots. In this evolving landscape, drones have emerged as promising solutions, particularly for indoor applications, due to their safety and efficiency advantages. Despite these advancements, challenges persist, especially in ineffective navigation and airspace management within indoor environments. To address this gap, this current study emphasizes on utilizing a convolutional neural network (CNN) for room number detection within indoor drone systems, which is essential for ensuring precise product delivery. The drone is equipped with a Pixhawk flight controller and a Raspberry Pi for image capture and processing using a CNN model implemented in Keras based on the collected data. Our CNN model has achieved a recognition accuracy of 92.4%, outperforming conventional models in recall and F1 Score, highlighting the effectiveness of CNN-based solutions for advancing indoor drone operations and improving delivery services. The integration of image processing into real-time recognition systems mounted on drones holds immense potential for enhancing delivery efficiency and accuracy. This research demonstrates the transformative capabilities of CNN-based solutions in advancing indoor drone operations, promising more reliable and efficient services in the future.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Wind Energy Harvesting Capacity of a Horizontal Axis Wind Turbine (HAWT) Using a Novel Wind Tracking System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: In this research, a new active wind tracking system is developed and the developed system is integrated with a HAWT. The wind tracking system possesses simple structure consisting angular displacement sensor, wind flag, microcontroller and dc servo motor in which less frictional elements and yaw error are accomplished. Several experiments have been conducted with the proposed setup (HAWT with wind tracking system) and the measured data were compared with that of the conventional HAWT (no wind tracking system). It is appeared that a HAWT with the developed wind tracking system could be one of the cleanness approaches to meet the energy demand in worldwide. The results revealed that the proposed setup could extract almost double wind energy of the conventional system for the case of wind attack angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$75^{\circ}$</tex>. The maximum position adjustment time was measured 1.39 seconds by the developed system. Moreover, the developed system maintained almost constant power outputs and rotor speed for all angle of wind attack during the experiments. The experimental results and data of this research could be a potential of exploring the economic aspect of the proposed system in future.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Sentiment Classification on IMDB 50k Movie Reviews: A Study Using CNN, LSTM, CNN-LSTM, and BERT Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Sentiment analysis of movie reviews plays a critical role in understanding audience perception and informing marketing strategies in the film industry. This study investigates the effectiveness of various deep learning models for sentiment classification on the IMDB 50k movie review dataset and compares the performance of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, a combined CNN-LSTM architecture, and pre-trained transformer models like BERT and RoBERTa, coupled with Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). The research explores the impact of pre-processing techniques like text cleaning, tokenization, and embedding on model performance. Hyperparameter optimization is employed to fine-tune each model for optimal accuracy. Metrics such as precision, accuracy, recall, and Fl-score are employed to evaluate the performance of each model in categorizing movie reviews into positive or negative sentiments. The findings reveal that RoBERTa+DNN achieved the highest performance with an accuracy of 0.9205, followed closely by BERT+DNN at 0.9135. While CNN and LSTM models achieved good accuracy (0.8847 and 0.8602 respectively), they were surpassed by the combined CNN-LSTM architecture (0.8851) and the pre-trained transformer models. It identifies RoBERTa+DNN as the most effective model for classifying IMDB movie reviews, achieving the highest Fl-score (0.9217). This study contributes through the integration of BERT and RoBERTa models with Dense Nets to enhance sentiment classification results, alongside comprehensive comparisons with various es-tablished classification models. The research also emphasizes the importance of pre-processing techniques and hyperparameter optimization in achieving optimal model performance.

articleTitle: IoT Revolution: Exploring the Impact of loT Based Embedded System Technology on Healthcare, Agriculture and Business Startups in Smart Village
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The paper illustrates the development of an integrated Internet of Things (IoT) gadget with smart agricultural and healthcare systems, as well as the possibility for their startup firms to build a smart village. The system comprises a carefully designed front end powered by Arduino and NodeMCU microcontrollers. It has a number of high-precision sensors, including the DS18B20 for body temperature, the Max30102 for heart rate and oxygen level, the FC-28 for soil moisture, the DHT-11 for temperature of the environment and maintaining humidity, the dust sensor for air quality detection, and calibrated MQ sensors for gas detection of CH4, H2S, and NH3. The back end simply interfaces with the Blynk application, ThingSpeak, and Google spreadsheet as data storage for detailed data visualization and real-time monitoring via smart devices. A rigorous sensor validation process that was carried out, indicating that this device's measurements align statistically with those of commercially available sensors, as validated by paired sample t-tests, Q-Q plot and descriptive data analysis in SPSS software. The prototypic data analysis system is also a key aspect of this research. Our proposed research not only supports the usefulness of our technology, but also gives a direction for future users to correctly evaluate their data. The integrated IoT device exhibits its utilization for smart healthcare and precision agriculture systems for the purpose of smart village. The combination of IoT along with startup enterprises is extending unique notions that could improve global food sustainability and individual well-being. This paper displays the potential for startups to develop innovative IoT, health, and agriculture solutions that will shape a future where technology improves lives and ensures food security.

articleTitle: An Approach to Automatic Leaf Recognition of Bangladeshi Plants Using Image Processing Techniques and Random Forests
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This study proposes a novel approach for identi-fying plant leaves using a combination of handcrafted visual leaf image features(shape, color, texture, and preliminary vein properties), their extraction strategies (based on image processing and statistical measures), and classification methods. To do so, a 5-step approach is presented comprising image acquisition, image pre-processing, feature extraction, classification steps, comparison, and evaluation. The presented approach is tested on publicly available standard leaf image datasets such as Flavia, Swedish, and our self-collected BDLeaf20 dataset comprising 20 Bangladeshi local plant species which include fruit, flower, and medicinal plants bearing a total of 1072 leaf images. The plant species included in the BDleaf20 dataset vary in terms of their rarity and popularity within the region. To investigate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, Random Forests classifier is used achieving accuracy scores of 97.21 %,99.11 %, and 93.17% respectively on the Flavia, Swedish, and BDLeaf20 datasets.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Highway Vehicle Tracking Using Different Object Trackers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Radar is a crucial technology widely used across various sectors, including the military, defense, space exploration, environmental monitoring, and traffic control. This paper presents advancements in radar technology, focusing on extended object tracking and multipath radar reflections to enhance tracking and classification accuracy in challenging environments such as heavy rain, fog, and dense traffic. We explore two main systems: the first employs parametric variation in object tracking to reduce false alarms and errors, significantly improving the tracking performance. The second system leverages multipath radar reflections, where parametric adjustments have led to a notable increase in target detection accuracy (91.42%). This improvement is particularly vital for applications requiring precise target identification, such as autonomous driving and vehicle tracking, ensuring safer and more efficient operations. Our results demonstrate the effectiveness of parametric modeling in optimizing radar systems for better reliability and robustness in diverse applications. This research contributes to the development of safer transportation systems and more accurate environmental sensing, showcasing the potential of advanced radar technologies in addressing realworld challenges.

articleTitle: A Recuced Switch Z-Armed Multi Level Inverter for Grid Connected PV System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: The Z-arm multilevel inverter topology is characterized by its cascaded structure, which consists of multiple H-bridge or half-bridge cells connected in series. Each cell employs a separate DC source, typically capacitors or batteries, allowing for precise voltage control and scalability to higher voltage levels. The arrangement of the cells in a Z-shaped configuration enables a modular and compact design, facilitating easy integration into various power electronic systems. The main objective of Z-arm multilevel inverters is their ability to generate high-quality output waveforms with reduced harmonic content. This is achieved through the utilization of multiple voltage levels, which provide finer voltage resolution and smoother transitions between voltage steps. A selective harmonic elimination (SHE) have been developed to enhance the performance of Z-arm multilevel inverters. Further the proposed inverter is tested on 2.5kW grid connected PV system to validate its performance according the THD standards of IEEE519.

articleTitle: Advanced Optical Quantum Computing Using Liquid Crystal Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: We review recent research in various types of optical quantum computing using liquid crystal (LC) devices. First, we have investigated Young's Interference experiment using self-aligned LC devices and a logical “NOT” operation is achieved. Second, numerical quantization of interfering small photons using a LC retarder is investigated. Third, a Mach-Zehnder interferometer with an optical phase control by a twisted nematic (TN) LC device was studied. Fourth, 4-bit optical path linear quantum computation using Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm with the LC device as a linear optical element was investigated.

articleTitle: 3D CNN with Attention Modules for Enhanced COVID-19 and Pneumonia Screening from CT Scans
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: During the COVID-19 outbreak, deep-learning techniques have been extensively studied for computer-assisted diagnosis. However, distinguishing COVID-19 from other types of pneumonia remains challenging. This research describes an automated chest CT imaging technique for COVID-19 pneumonia screening. CT scans provide valuable three-dimensional information, aiding in detecting COVID-19 symptoms. The limited availability of comprehensive 3D datasets has slowed the use of attention-based models in this field. To address this, we propose a novel 3D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a residual block incorporating self-attention and spatial attention modules. Our primary goal is accurately classifying COVID-19 and pneumonia cases based on CT scans. Integrating attention modules enhances spatial correlation analysis across CT slices, enabling dynamic re-calibration of the CNN output to identify complex patterns. Training our <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3D$</tex> CNN on CT scan images from the CC-CCII dataset achieved an impressive accuracy rate of 99.42%. Subsequently, we used the CNN's prediction probabilities to construct feature vectors for each sample. By training various machine learning classifiers independently and combining them through soft voting, we achieved a remarkable 98.66% accuracy. This study highlights how our approach can improve pulmonary patient care and diagnostic processes, leveraging state-of-the-art deep learning techniques for accurate and efficient COVID-19 pneumonia screening.

articleTitle: A Cost-Effective Approach to Bengali Handwritten Character Recognition with Custom Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Handwritten character identification is a crucial area in pattern recognition and image processing, given its broad range of applications. Although extensive research has been conducted on English character recognition, there is a noticeable gap in studies focusing on Bengali characters. This paper proposes a systematic method for recognizing Bengali characters. Our approach leverages a convolutional neural net-work (CNN) architecture designed specifically to manage the intricate structure of the Bengali language. Unlike previous studies, which often rely on larger datasets, our approach centers on focused experimentation using a curated dataset of 3,000 character samples. The recognition technique encompasses segmentation, feature extraction, and classification, emphasizing the latest advancements in CNN-based text detection for English characters. Notably, our research extends these techniques to Bengali handwritten characters, demonstrating the versatility and efficacy of our approach. Experimental results from our cu-rated dataset and CMATERdb 3.1.2, carefully divided for testing and training, were promising. We show that our model effectively identifies handwritten Bengali characters, as evidenced by high accuracy rates of 95.67% and 93.83%, respectively, with only 0.8 million parameters based on the number of output classes. The aforementioned results underscore the methodology's potential for both practical applications and future research projects.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of the Old Solar Module Performance Degradation under Outdoor Weather Conditions in Bangladesh: A Visual and Electrical Investigation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This research investigates the performance degradation of six 10-watt photovoltaic (PV) modules after five years of exposure to the humid climate of Bangladesh. Employing a comprehensive approach, the research conducted visual and electrical analyses to provide a holistic understanding of the modules’ conditions. Visual inspection, involving top and rear views, revealed various degradation factors, including discoloration, delamination, back sheet damage, corrosion, and dust and soiling. Simultaneously, electrical performance was evaluated using an I-V tracer outdoors, and experimental results demonstrated the degradation of the modules over time. A 9.614-watt maximum and a 5.665-watt minimum output power were found for the old PV panel. The greatest yearly deterioration rate among the six panels was 8.67%, and the lowest degradation rate was 0.77%. The maximum and minimum percentage degradation rates over five years were 43.35% and 3.86%, respectively. We assessed the extent of performance decline by comparing the obtained data with the manufacturer's specifications. This work emphasizes the correlation between visual anomalies and electrical degradation, shedding light on the interplay of these factors.

articleTitle: Optimizing Community Energy with Smart Hardware Integration in Offline Microgrid Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: This paper introduces a simple yet powerful plan to bring uninterrupted electricity to local communities by offering an optimized IoT-based off-grid microgrid system. The project integrates diverse renewable sources-solar, Aeromine (wind), and piezo-tech-into a micro-grid to ensure uninterrupted power supply. The integration of the IoT (Internet of Things) based monitoring system, such as Blynk application, allows for remote monitoring and control of the microgrid, providing a timely response to any potential issues. Additionally, our advanced battery technology not only improves energy storage efficiency but also enhances the reliability and stability of the microgrid. A backup generator is used to ensure the supply of electricity when all the other sources are down, ensuring a day-and-night power supply for the load demand. Finally, by incorporating the HOMER (Hybrid Optimization of Multiple Electric Renewables) software suite, we optimized our microgrid design for maximum reliability and efficiency. The findings highlight critical hardware choices, including a storage power capital cost of BDT 10,850,000 and a wind power investment of BDT 6,000,000. The energy mix ensures efficient production throughout the day, meeting a load demand of 166 kW/day with real-time monitoring functionalities. This approach offers a promising model for large-scale sustainable electrification, advancing community electrification strategies.

articleTitle: Gene Expression Programming-Based Gas Reservoir Porosity Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Porosity is one of the essential properties of a reservoir rock, which relates to the volume of void space in a reservoir rock. It significantly impacts the calculation of hydrocarbon reserves and petroleum economics, making it a key petrophysical characteristic of the rock. The conventional techniques for determining porosity are time-consuming and costly. As a result, different approaches have been developed to predict porosity. The major aims of this study are i) to construct a gene expression programming (GEP)-based porosity model and ii) develop a correlation to obtain rock porosity. Through extensive analysis and experimentation, the GEP-based model is shown to be effective in accurately predicting porosity. A total number of 183 datasets, with four input variables and single output response, are randomly divided into 129 and 54 data sets for training and testing to develop the model, respectively. According to the simulated results with GEP, the prediction shows of mean absolute percentage error and a high correlation coefficient of 0.5% and 94.14 %, for the testing phase, respectively. GEP has a strong potential for predicting the reservoir porosity in the considered parameters. This research strategy can be applied to predict the reservoir rock and fluid properties for oil and gas reservoir characterization and simulation studies.

articleTitle: Designing a Double Integral Sliding Mode Controller for Battery Storage and Wind - Based DC Microgrids with ANN-MPPT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: A double integral sliding mode control (DISMC) scheme has been proposed in this paper to ensure the regulation of the DC-bus voltage. The proposed DCMG consists of a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG)-based wind farm along with a battery energy storage systems (BESSs) to improve the sustainability. An artificial neural network (ANN) is used to extract maximum power from PMSG unit. The proposed control architecture assures the optimal power sharing among the DCMG's components by controlling the power converters associated with it. The entire stability of the system has also been guaranteed by employing this proposed controller. Furthermore, the resilience of the proposed control scheme is proven via the control Lyapunov theory. Finally, the performance of the suggested DISMC approach is contrasted with an existing sliding mode controller (ESMC) focusing on tracking efficiency of DC-bus voltage, settling time, and overshoot through Matlab/Simulink simulations. The processor-in-the-loop (PIL) is utilized to validate the practical deployment of the proposed control technique.

articleTitle: Transforming Leukemia Classification: A Comprehensive Study on Deep Learning Models for Enhanced Diagnostic Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Leukemia is a severe form of blood cancer that presents significant challenges in both diagnosis and treatment. Early and accurate detection is crucial for successful patient outcomes, but traditional diagnostic methods relying on pathologist expertise can be subjective and time-consuming. This can lead to delays in identifying the appropriate treatment plan, especially given the complexity of accurately categorizing leukemia subtypes. To address these challenges, a study has been conducted to comprehensively evaluate Deep Learning (DL) techniques for leukemia classification. The study compares the performance of conventional Machine Learning (ML) methods with cutting-edge Transfer Learning (TL) models across multiclass scenarios. The study employed Laplacian of Gaussian-based Modified High-boosting (LoGMH) for image enhancement, along with image augmentation techniques such as brightness and rotation adjustments to expand the dataset. Additionally, feature extraction using the gray-level run length matrix (GLRLM) was applied to improve feature representation. Among the models tested, Inception-ResNet emerged as the top performer, achieving an accuracy of 95.52% and an F1 score of 95.49% in distinguishing five leukemia subtypes. This research underscores the potential of TL models in advancing medical diagnostics, particularly in the early detection and precise classification of leukemia, thereby enhancing patient care in hematology and oncology. The future research will focus on integrating additional clinical data, validating models in diverse clinical environments, and emphasizing model transparency and interpretability.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Classification by Ensemble Learning Utilizing Wavelet Transformation-based Statistical Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Brain tumors are regarded as highly dangerous and severe conditions, frequently leading to a substantial reduction in life expectancy. Accurate identification of brain tumors is essential for developing successful therapies that can increase patients' chances of survival. The process of manually examining and interpreting extensive MRI data can be both complex and labor-intensive. As a result of this, there is a pressing need for a trustworthy machine-learning method for accurately identifying brain tumors, and during the last decade, many approaches have been implemented. This research presents a novel method to identify as abnormal any given MR brain image. The proposed method begins with the application of DWT to extract features from images. To find the most pertinent features, PCA is then applied as a feature selection method. These selected features are classified using both a SVM with a polynomial kernel and an Ensemble of Decision Trees (EoDT), with k-fold cross-validation employed to improve the model's generalizability. Our proposed methods demonstrate enhanced performance, with the EoDT model attaining the maximum classification accuracy of 99.95%. The SVM model obtains an accuracy of 90.61%, while the combined model reaches an accuracy of 94.20%. The experimental data indicate that the method is both effective and efficient, making it suitable for brain tumor classification. It can assist doctors in diagnosing whether a patient is normal or abnormal to varying degrees.

articleTitle: Effective Pest Detection by YOLOv5 with BottleneckCSP
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Pest damage poses a significant risk to crop quality and productivity, underscoring the necessity for accurate and efficient detection methods for farmers. Artificial intelligence (AI) facilitates targeted pest management with reduced reliance on broad-spectrum insecticides and enables early detection of insect infestations. Object detection, a computer vision approach, is revolutionizing pest identification in agriculture by locating pests in digital crop photographs. However, the detection of tiny objects within these datasets presents challenges due to sparse spatial information. In response to this challenge, we have replaced the C3 block of YOLOv5 with the BottleneckCSP module, which is more effective for feature mapping of tiny objects. Our enhanced model demonstrates superior performance on the IP102 dataset, which is characterized by the presence of tiny objects. Comparative analysis reveals that our BottleneckCSP-integrated model significantly improves feature mapping, resulting in a notable increase in mean average precision (mAP). Specifically, our modified model achieves an mAP of 63.9%, outperforming many state-of-the-art methods on this dataset. This advancement in the YOLOv5 architecture sets a new benchmark for AI-powered precision agriculture, providing farmers with a highly efficient tool for crop protection and pest management. The significant performance gains highlight the potential of our approach to transform current agricultural practices, paving the way for more sustainable and effective pest control strategies.

articleTitle: Cloud-Based Ceiling Robot Assisted Intelligent Warehouse Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Driven by the surge in online shopping, warehouses are expanding and evolving, but often grapple with limited storage and inefficient use of space due to flawed layouts and outdated technologies. It was seen that heavier products take more time to deliver. To address these challenges, a new research proposes a cloud-based, ceiling-mounted robot. This innovative system dispatches from the ceiling, swiftly picking and delivering products in an average of 30.11 seconds. Thanks to its unique eight-wheel mechanism, the robot boasts auto-steering capabilities, exceptional stability, and impressive load capacity (170 grams) while maintaining low power consumption (2 Watts). Operated wirelessly via the web or app, the system empowers users to control stocking and delivery, enhancing adaptability and efficiency in modern warehouses. The proposed solution addresses the issues of inefficient product delivery times and space utilization, significantly improving warehouse operations.

articleTitle: RAD-U-Net: Residual Attention-Based Dual-Path U-Net for Segmentation of Multiple Myeloma Cells in Microscopic Images for Clinical Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Multiple myeloma, a malignancy originating in the bone marrow, poses significant health risks and can lead to severe systemic dysfunction and potentially fatal outcomes. Manual microscopic analysis of multiple myeloma cells remains a cornerstone in the diagnosis of this disease. However, this process is labor-intensive, time-consuming, and prone to human error. To address these challenges, we propose a novel approach leveraging advanced image processing and deep learning techniques for automated segmentation of multiple myeloma cells from microscopic images. We build a novel Residual Attention-based Dual-path U-Net architecture tailored specifically for this task. Our approach leverages deep learning techniques, including dual pathways for feature extraction with residual and attention mechanisms, to precisely detect multiple myeloma cells from complex microscopic images. Through rigorous experimentation, our model achieves outstanding segmentation performance, with a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 91.50%, a dice score of 95.44%, mean average precision (mAP) of 96.46%. Despite its lightweight design, with only 5.7 million parameters, our model demonstrates remarkable accuracy as mentioned above, showcasing its potential for real-world clinical applications. Additionally, our proposed architecture maintains a balance between segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency because of reduced parameter, making it a more practical and effective solution for cell segmentation tasks, especially in scenarios where computational resources are limited or efficiency is a priority. However, there remains potential for further improvement in certain metrics, such as the mIoU and mAP, suggesting opportunities for refining the model to achieve even better segmentation accuracy.

articleTitle: An Early Diabetes Detection Framework Utilizing Interpretable Hybrid Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Power, Electrical, Electronics and Industrial Applications (PEEIACON)
abstract: Diagnosing diabetes, a chronic metabolic disorder distinguished by heightened levels of glucose in the blood, presents substantial obstacles and presents considerable health hazards. Detection of diabetes that is both accurate and efficient is vital for timely intervention and management. Utilizing a binary tabular dataset, we present an innovative interpretable hybrid deep learning model proposed in this study. Our methodology incorporates a stacked ensemble model (EM) that consists of Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), Random Forest (RF), and Naive Bayes (NB) as base-classifiers, in addition to an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) functioning as the meta-classifier. By capitalizing on the respective merits of conventional machine learning (ML) algorithms and deep learning methodologies, this amalgamation seeks to improve the precision of predictions and the resilience of models. In order to effectively address the crucial requirement for interpretability in medical diagnostic models, we have utilized SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values. These values provide valuable insights into the decision-making process of our model and highlight the specific contribution of each feature to the final prediction outcome. The effectiveness of the proposed model in detecting diabetes has been substantiated through a comprehensive evaluation of its performance utilizing a range of metrics. The proposed model has achieved 99.22% accuracy.
